PT/FM OWNER'S MANUAL

POCKET TRACKER / FUSION MACHINE

for PT/FM 0.26

BY HITOSU

About this manual

PT/FM is a firmware for the M-VAVE FM-1. It turns the FM-1 into a tracker: you write music as patterns of notes, play them as songs, stack live loops, mix two songs like a DJ, and play six kinds of instrument from its keys.

Read chapters 1 to 5 first: they install PT/FM, show the panel, explain the few rules every screen follows, and walk you through your first hour. Chapters 6 to 15 explain each screen in detail. The rest of the manual is for looking things up: every shortcut, every message, troubleshooting, the instruments that come with PT/FM, the specifications, and a glossary of the words used (appendix G).

PT/FM's home is hitosu.github.io/ptfm: the latest version, its pages (the install page, the EDITOR page), the demo disk and this manual. Its source, free software, is at github.com/hitosu/ptfm.

In a hurry? Install PT/FM and the demo disk (chapter 2), then go straight to chapter 5: it plays a song in a minute, and names every key it uses.

The FM-1 also has its own help on every screen: press HOME + LFO. Its pages are short reminders of what this manual explains.

How this manual writes things

WrittenMeans
SEQa button or a knob, by the name printed on the panel. PLAY is the button printed PLAY / STOP.
POLYa black key, by the name printed on it. The last black key has no print: this manual calls it the blank key.
3a white key, counted from the left: white key 1 is the lowest, white key 16 the highest.
HOME + LFOa combination: the first button held (or, for HOME, tapped first), then the second.
PLAY heldpressed and kept down for a moment (half a second unless you set HOLD DELAY otherwise).
SEL held + K1the same, said where the holding matters: keep SEL down and turn K1.
HOME + white key helda combination whose last key is kept down (here, the white key). "Held" after a combination is always about its last key.
SAVEDa message the FM-1 shows, exactly as it shows it. Numbers in messages change with the case (TRACK 02 MUTED).

On the web page on a computer, point at a key in the text and it lights on the FM-1 drawn beside the text; a row of a key table lights all its keys. Point at a key or knob of the drawing and its screen names it.

Numbers on the FM-1 are mostly hexadecimal, two digits: tracks 00 to 0F are the first to the sixteenth track, and patterns and cartridges count 00, 01 ... 09, 0A ... 0F, 10 and so on.

PT/FM at a glance

PT/FM stands for Pocket Tracker / Fusion Machine. It is a complete music workstation in the FM-1: write songs, play them, play over them live, and keep everything on the FM-1 itself.

What it does

  • A tracker. Music is written as patterns: a grid of up to 16 tracks across and up to 128 rows down, each row a step in time. A cell holds a note, the instrument that plays it, a volume and up to 4 commands (a slide, an arpeggio, a tempo change ...). A song plays patterns in an order of your choice. The EDITOR writes patterns; SONGS arranges them.
  • Six kinds of instrument, sharing one pool of voices; INSTRUMENTS picks, tries and edits them:
    • DX7: 6-operator FM, the classic digital synth.
    • JUNO-106: the classic analogue polysynth.
    • TB-303: the acid bass line, with slide and accent.
    • CHIP: the sound chips of 8-bit computers and consoles.
    • Sampler: recorded sounds, with loops and an envelope.
    • FUSION: an instrument made of a pattern, where one note is one pattern row. Each key plays its own row of the pattern (C-4 plays row 3C), every note written in that row at once, each on its own instrument: one key can play a chord, a layered sound, or a different drum on every key, a kit. The row's commands play as well, so a key can also start an arpeggio or a short riff (chapter 8).
  • Up to 16 notes at once (SETTINGS' VOICES: 8, 12 or 16), from the songs, the loops and the keys together.
  • Effects: GATE, FILTER, DRIVE, LO-FI, CHORUS, DELAY, REVERB, LIMITER and DUCK, each song with its own setup, plus a METRONOME. Held on the white keys, sixteen punch-in effects play over everything for as long as a key is down (FX).
  • LOOPS, a loop station: record up to 16 loops of one length on top of each other, mute and solo them from the keys, and record the whole performance as a new song (RECORD LIVE).
  • DJ: two songs on two decks, kept in time, mixed with a crossfader, with filters, pads and an LFO.
  • MIDI: play PT/FM from a keyboard or a computer (USB, or the TRS MIDI IN jack), learn an outside controller's knobs and pads onto the FM-1's own, send the keys and everything that plays out over USB, or make the FM-1 a controller for the computer (MIDI CONTROLLER).
  • Sync with other gear, three ways (chapter 16):
    • MIDI clock in (SETTINGS' SYNC EXTERNAL): PT/FM follows a sequencer's or a drum machine's clock, from USB or the MIDI IN jack, with its START, STOP, CONTINUE and song position, locked to it so nothing drifts.
    • MIDI clock out (CLOCK OUT ON): PT/FM leads, sending the clock, START / STOP / CONTINUE and the song position over USB.
    • Audio sync pulse (SETTINGS' OUTPUT SYNC PULSE L or R): a click on one side of the output every half beat, for instruments that follow a sync pulse, the music in mono on the other side. It works while PT/FM leads (SYNC INTERNAL).
  • USB audio: a computer connected by USB hears PT/FM as a sound card and can record it.
  • Everything stays on the FM-1: SAVE writes your songs, patterns, instruments and settings into its own memory, where they survive power-off and firmware updates.

What comes with it

Built into the firmware are 11 synth cartridges, numbered F0 to FA: eight DX7 cartridges (F0 KEYS/ORGANS to F7 PERC/FX), F8 JUNO-106 (128 sounds), F9 CHIPTUNE (128 sounds) and FA TB-303 (64 sounds). They are always there, even on an empty FM-1. You can edit them like anything else; SAVE keeps your changes, and the originals come back with BACK TO BUILT-IN.

The demo disk is uploaded from the install page (chapter 2). It adds five sampler cartridges (a drum kit, percussion, band and orchestra instruments, voices, basses), the FUSION cartridge, six demo songs and twelve DJ loops. Appendix D lists them all.

The screens

PT/FM has ten screens. Each black key opens one (press HOME, then the black key), and FX has a button of its own:

KeyScreenFor
OP1SONGSyour songs: the list, and each song's order of patterns
OP2EDITORwriting patterns
OP3INSTRUMENTScartridges and instruments: choose, try, edit
OP4PLAYBACKfollowing what plays
OP5DJtwo songs mixed live
PITVISUALthe sound made visible
GLOSTATUSthe start screen: version, help, performance, storage
MONOSETTINGSsettings and tools

The black key OP6 and the blank key have no screen yet.

Installing and updating

PT/FM is installed from a web page, install.html, that comes with the firmware. It works offline: the firmware and the demo disk are inside the page. Get the latest from PT/FM's home, hitosu.github.io/ptfm, or from its repository, github.com/hitosu/ptfm (the dist folder).

Before you start

  • Open install.html in Chrome or Edge, on a computer or an Android phone. Safari and iPhones cannot talk MIDI from a web page.
  • Connect the FM-1 by USB and switch it on. Keep it connected until the page says it is done.
  • When the browser asks, allow MIDI devices, SysEx included: the whole install goes through MIDI.
Changes not yet saved on the FM-1 are lost by an install, as when it is switched off. Press SAVE on the FM-1 first.

INSTALL FIRMWARE

Writes PT/FM over whatever firmware the FM-1 runs.

  1. Open install.html and connect the FM-1.
  2. Press INSTALL FIRMWARE. The page shows its progress; the FM-1 restarts by itself.
  3. When the page says it is done, the FM-1 starts PT/FM on its STATUS screen.

Over PT/FM (an update), your songs, patterns, instruments, samples and settings stay where they are: the install writes nothing into PT/FM's own memory, the user area. Over another firmware, keep a copy of your work first: other firmwares erase that memory when they are installed. The EDITOR page saves the FM-1's whole library to a file (chapter 17).

Updates: a new version comes as a new install page, on PT/FM's home. Install it as above; STATUS shows the version the FM-1 runs.

CLEAN INSTALL

A fresh start. With the CLEAN INSTALL switch on, INSTALL FIRMWARE writes PT/FM and then erases everything the FM-1 holds: your work, the settings, and any damaged records. The FM-1 then starts with an empty user area and only the built-in cartridges. Upload the demo disk after it if you want the demo songs.

The FM-1 can do the same erase on its own, without a computer: SETTINGS, TOOLS, FACTORY RESET (chapter 13).

UPLOAD DEMO DISK

Needs PT/FM running on the FM-1. Afterwards the FM-1 holds exactly the demo disk: its songs, patterns, cartridges and samples take the place of yours, and what of yours is not on it is gone.

It is a fresh start with the demo disk: everything you saved goes, your settings, MIDI mappings, loops, DJ's decks and your changes to the built-in cartridges included. Only the built-in cartridges themselves stay.

  • To keep your work, back it up first on the EDITOR page: READ, then DOWNLOAD DISK (chapter 17).
  • To add the demo songs to your own work instead of replacing it, drop demo.ptfmdsk on the EDITOR page's TABLE, drag what you want onto its FM-1 panel, and WRITE.
  • If the FM-1 has edits not saved, the upload is refused: press SAVE on the FM-1 (or revert them), then upload again.
  • An upload cut short leaves what was there whole, unless the upload was replacing a nearly full FM-1's library: then part of it may be left. Either way, upload again. The FM-1 says what it found when it starts.

USB RESCUE

If the FM-1 does not start, or does not answer the install page:

  1. Switch the FM-1 off.
  2. Hold OCT- and switch it on. The screen says USB RESCUE.
  3. Press INSTALL FIRMWARE on the install page.

The FM-1 also starts in USB RESCUE by itself after two failed starts in a row.

An install cut short (a cable pulled, the power lost) is not resumed by itself. Press INSTALL FIRMWARE again. If the FM-1 no longer answers the page, switch it off and start it in USB RESCUE (OCT- held at power-on), then install from there.

If something goes wrong

  • No FM-1 found: close what else uses its MIDI port (a music program, another installer, another browser tab), then try again.
  • Back to another firmware: PT/FM keeps the FM-1's update path, so another FM-1 firmware's installer replaces it, from USB RESCUE if need be.

The panel

Seven endless knobs and a volume knob, fourteen buttons, 27 keys and a 240 × 240 colour screen. Many of the buttons are printed for the FM-1's original synth; PT/FM gives each one job on every screen.

Knobs and buttons

ControlIts job
1 MASTERThe volume. It is a plain volume knob, never used for anything else.
2 SELECTMoves the cursor up and down (rows, list items).
3 PRESETSPicks the current instrument, on every screen: the sound the keys play.
4 ALGORITHMMoves the cursor left and right (tracks, columns).
5-8 K1 K2 K3 K4Change values at the cursor. The footer says what each one turns. (Printed KNOB1 to KNOB4.)
9, 10 OCT- OCT+The keys' octave, -4 to +4.
11 FXThe FX screen. Held with a white key: a punch-in effect.
12 SELSelect and act: the menu of the thing at the cursor. Held, a shift.
13 ENVThe lists: patterns, cartridges, samples, songs (read it as Explore Named Vaults).

15 EDITOpen the thing at the cursor for editing; again, done.
16 GLOThe properties of what the screen shows: the song, the pattern, the view.
17 HOMEBack. At the top of a screen: the screens, mutes, rewind and help (HOME's combination).
18 SAVEWrite every change to the FM-1's memory.
19 ARPThe arpeggiator (Again, Repeat, Please).
20 SEQThe screen's next view (Show Else, Quick).
21 PLAYPlay / pause. Held: stop and go back to the start.

The keys

The 27 keys play notes, F-3 to G-5 at octave 0; OCT- and OCT+ shift them down to C-0 or up to G-9. At octave -4 the seven lowest keys, which would be below C-0, are silent. Many screens give the keys other jobs:

  • The 16 white keys are 16 tracks, 16 loops, 16 steps or 16 punch-in effects, depending on the screen. White key 1 is the leftmost.
  • The 11 black keys open the screens (with HOME): OP1 to OP5, PIT, GLO, MONO and POLY. OP6 and the last, unprinted key, the blank key, have no screen yet.
KeyWith HOME, opens
1 OP1SONGS (Open Page 1)
2 OP2EDITOR
3 OP3INSTRUMENTS
4 OP4PLAYBACK
5 OP5DJ
6 OP6nothing yet
7 PITVISUAL (Pictures In Time)
8 GLOSTATUS
9 MONOSETTINGS (My Own Nerdy Options)
10 POLYLOOPS (Party On, Loop Yourself)
11 BLANKnothing yet
12 white keystracks to mute or solo (HOME's combination)

Without HOME, some screens give the black keys jobs of their own: on DJ they work the two decks, on FX LIVE each picks an effect (and the blank key is BYPASS), on LOOPS' CONTROL mode they set the quantize and the next loops' mode. Each screen's chapter lists them.

The lights

Every button and key has a light, and the lights tell you what works:

  • dim: it does something on this screen;
  • off: it does nothing here;
  • on: its mode or its list is open (REC on: writing; ARP on: the arpeggiator runs).

PLAY has two lights. Green means playing (brighter on each beat); red means paused. Green with a dim red means a loop is playing (the EDITOR's pattern or the loops), not a song. Red dim alone: nothing to resume yet. Both dark: PLAY has nothing to play here.

Some lights have rules of their own:

  • SAVE is dim while something is not saved yet, dark when everything is saved, and blinks dim while a save waits for the music to pause.
  • OCT- and OCT+ show the octave. Both are dark at octave 0; OCT- lights for the octaves below, OCT+ for those above: dim at 1, full at 2, blinking slowly at 3 and fast at 4.
  • A fast blink on a button means it cannot act just now: PLAY with no song to play, for example.
  • HOME breathes (dim to full and back) while HOME's combination is open; then the black keys show the screens (the current one bright, the others dim, OP6 and the blank key dark) and the white keys show the tracks: dim while a track plays, dark while it is muted, bright while it is soloed.
  • REC is on while the EDITOR writes, and blinks during a take.
  • The keys light with their notes: full while a note is loud, dim as it fades, dark once it is quiet. A plucked sound flashes and fades, a held pad stays lit, so the keys show what sounds, not only what is pressed.
  • While FX is held (and on FX LIVE) the white keys are the punch-ins: keys 1, 5, 9 and 13 light dim so you can find each group of four by touch, and a running punch-in lights full. Other screens that use the white keys as buttons (steps, DJ's pads) light them the same way.

The screen

Every screen has the same frame:

  • The header (the top line): the screen's name in its group's colour, then what it shows (a pattern's number, a page, SEQ and the view SEQ switches to); on the right the voices sounding, the transport (a green triangle playing, two red bars paused, a red dot recording), the processor's load and the battery. The battery has three bars, its shell turning red when none is left; while a computer powers the FM-1 over USB, the bars fill one after another in light blue (a plain USB charger cannot be told apart, so it shows the battery). Short messages (toasts) take the name's place for two seconds, and so does a knob's name and value while you turn it.
  • The footer (the bottom line): on the left the current instrument, the one the keys play (F8:00 and its name: cartridge F8, slot 00); on the right what the knobs turn here.
  • The body between them: the screen's own content.

The colours (in the DEFAULT theme; other themes keep the same roles):

ColourMeans
light reda DX7 instrument, its notes
light cyana JUNO-106 instrument, its notes
light greena TB-303 instrument, its notes
light bluea CHIP instrument, its notes; commands in a cell (at its right, where notes never stand); the MAKE screens' names
yellowa sampler instrument, its notes; samples; something not saved; keys in the help
light magentaa FUSION instrument, its notes
brownvolumes in a cell; a built-in item's number in a list; the HEAR screens' names
greenplaying, on, done; the PLAY screens' names
redrecording, a warning, an instrument that is missing
magentathe SYSTEM screens' names
dark greyempty: an empty cell's dots
The help (HOME + LFO) colours keys yellow, just as this manual sets them apart.

Basic operation

A few rules work the same on every screen. Learn them once and every screen is easy: HOME takes you around, PLAY plays, SAVE keeps your work, the knobs move and change, and every button acts when you let it go.

HOME: back, and to everywhere

HOME backs out of whatever is open: a menu, a list, an edit, a dialog. At the top of a screen, with nothing to back out of, a tap opens HOME's combination: HOME breathes, the keys that work light up, and the next key you press does one of these:

After HOMEDoes
HOME + OP1Opens SONGS, the list of your songs.
HOME + OP2Opens the EDITOR, where you write patterns.
HOME + OP3Opens INSTRUMENTS, where you pick and edit sounds.
HOME + OP4Opens PLAYBACK, which follows what plays.
HOME + OP5Opens DJ, two songs mixed live.
HOME + PITOpens VISUAL, the sound made visible.
HOME + GLOOpens STATUS, the start screen.
HOME + MONOOpens SETTINGS.
HOME + POLYOpens LOOPS, the loop station.
FXOpens FX, the effects. FX has a button of its own, so it needs no HOME.
HOME + SELECTTurns through the screens, one a click, round: STATUS, SONGS, EDITOR, INSTRUMENTS, PLAYBACK, VISUAL, FX, LOOPS, DJ, SETTINGS, and round again. Press HOME again to stay on the screen shown.
HOME + white keyMutes or unmutes a track: white key 1 is track 00, white key 16 track 0F (TRACK 02 MUTED, TRACK 02 ON). Key after key, while it stays open. In LOOPS the white keys are the loops (chapter 14); on DJ, keys 1-8 the left deck's tracks, 9-16 the right deck's (chapter 10).
HOME + white key heldSolos the track instead (TRACK 02 SOLO). The same on the soloed track ends the solo (SOLO OFF); on another track it moves the solo there.
HOME + SEQ + white keySEQ first switches the white keys to SOLO (and back to MUTE): then a tap solos.
HOME + PLAYRewinds what plays (or played last) to its start: BACK TO THE START (below). On DJ both decks go back to their cue points (BACK TO THE CUES, chapter 10).
HOME + RECThe CUT: all sound off at once (below).
HOME + LFOThe help for this screen, LOOK FOR ONSWERS (below).
HOMECloses the combination; at a menu, a list or an edit, backs out of it.
HOME heldOpens the same combination at once, for as long as it is held: HOME held + a black key goes to a screen, and so on.

While the combination is open, the white keys show the tracks: dim while a track plays, dark while it is muted, bright while it is soloed. The black keys show the screens, the current one bright.

Mutes and solos are part of the performance: they are not saved with the song. Once the combination has done something (a mute, say), any other key closes it and does its own job.

Playing and stopping

There is one transport: one thing plays at a time, the current song, the EDITOR's pattern loop, the loops or DJ's decks. PLAY acts the moment it is pressed.

  • On SONGS, the EDITOR, LOOPS and DJ, PLAY plays that screen's own thing: the song picked, the pattern shown (looped, from the cursor's row), the loops, both decks. If something else plays, it switches at once.
  • On the other screens, PLAY pauses and resumes whatever played last, so on FX or VISUAL it toggles what you hear.
  • What plays plays on from screen to screen until something else starts. Every edit is heard at once.
  • PLAY held stops: what plays goes back to its start, so the next PLAY plays it from the beginning (BACK TO THE START).
  • With no song to play, PLAY blinks: NO SONG TO PLAY.

The CUT: all sound off

HOME + REC, on every screen, stops every sound at once: notes, echoes, reverb tails. While REC is held there is no sound at all (SOUND CUT: LET GO OF REC), but what plays keeps its time; let go, it is heard again from its next notes.

Keep REC held for 2 seconds and every effect of what plays is switched off too (SOUND CUT, EFFECTS OFF). That is an edit like any other: SAVE keeps it, REVERT undoes it.

Saving your work

Every edit goes into the FM-1's working memory first and is heard at once. SAVE writes all of them to its flash memory, where they survive power-off. Switching off loses unsaved edits.

  • The SAVE light is dim while something is not saved.
  • A save shows its progress (SAVING 3 CHANGES), then SAVED. With nothing to save: NOTHING TO SAVE.
  • SAVE while playing waits for a pause (SAVE WAITS FOR A PAUSE); SAVE blinks meanwhile. A save still waiting is lost if the FM-1 is switched off.
  • REVERT, in a screen's SEL menu, takes the thing that screen shows back to what was saved (a pattern, a song, a cartridge, the loops ...), after a question: REVERTED.
  • REVERT ALL drops every edit since the last save: SAVE + OCT-, or SETTINGS, TOOLS, REVERT ALL. It asks first, then reloads: REVERTED TO SAVED (NOTHING TO REVERT when there is nothing).
  • SAVE held alone only shows what it does with other keys; let go then, it saves nothing. SAVE + OCT+ saves.
There is no undo step by step. What an edit changed only REVERT takes back, to what was saved. So the big actions ask first.

What SAVE keeps, and what switching off forgets:

SAVE keepsNever saved: gone at power-off
Your songs, with their order, properties, mixer and effectsTrack mutes and solos, and a loop's solo
Your patterns, and the EDITOR's own patternSONGS' play mode (ONE PLAY, REPEAT SONG, PLAY NEXT)
Your cartridges, and your changes to the built-in onesPLAYBACK's speed and volume
The settings, the MIDI map and your GATE patternsThe clipboards (blocks, slots)
The loops, with their mutes; DJ's decks as they standThe pattern recorder's steps
THE KEYS' setup and tempoThe arpeggiator being on, and the octave (SETTINGS' KEYS OCTAVE sets the octave at power-on)
The current instrument, and the pattern the EDITOR is onWhat was playing, and where

Samples are the one exception to "SAVE writes": CLONE and MOVE of a sampler cartridge write its samples at once.

A power cut during a save loses nothing that was saved before: the FM-1 keeps either the old state or the new one, whole. The same holds when the battery runs out.

The memory for edits holds what differs from what is saved (about 650 changed tracks). When it runs low, the header reminds you: SAVE CHANGES TO FREE MEMORY. When it is full, an edit that needs more is not made and a question asks you to save (MEMORY FOR EDITS IS FULL, SAVE BEFORE MAKING MORE EDITS): OCT+ SAVE NOW, OCT- back. After the save, make the edit again.

Storage full: a save that does not fit writes nothing and asks (NOT ENOUGH STORAGE TO SAVE): OCT+ runs CLEAN UP, which offers to delete unused patterns, samples and instruments; or delete something yourself and save again. Your edits stay in memory meanwhile. STATUS shows the free storage.

Things that use other things

A note uses an instrument, a song uses patterns, a FUSION instrument uses a pattern, a sampler instrument uses a sample. Moving, swapping or deleting something in use asks first (PATTERN 1A IS USED 3 TIMES, UPDATE REFERENCES?):

  • YES (OCT+): everything that used it follows the change, and everything is saved at once (UPDATING 3 REFERENCES, then REFERENCES UPDATED, SAVED).
  • NO (OCT-): the change is made, and what used it keeps the old number, now pointing at whatever is there.
  • HOME: nothing happens.

A reference to something missing is drawn in red and plays nothing. SETTINGS, TOOLS, CHECK REFERENCES lists them.

Built-in things

The built-in cartridges (F0 to FA) live in the firmware. Their numbers are brown wherever they are listed. You can play, use and edit them like anything else: SAVE keeps your changed copy under the same number, and it is used from then on, also after a firmware update. BACK TO BUILT-IN, in the cartridge list's SEL menu, brings the firmware's own back (CARTRIDGE F0 BUILT-IN AGAIN). Built-in things cannot be moved or deleted.

Taps, holds and combinations

  • Most buttons act when you let them go (a tap), so they can also be held as a modifier. PLAY, REC and the KEYS act the moment they are pressed, for timing.
  • Held + another control is a combination: SEL + K1 means keep SEL down and turn K1. The combination repeats while the button stays held (turn on and on), and the held button's own tap does not happen.
  • A slack of 0.1 s: a button let go a moment early still counts (SETTINGS' COMBO GRACE). So buttons that can combine act about 0.1 s after you let them go, and HOME then LFO can never clear a cell by mistake.
  • A button held alone past the hold delay (half a second, SETTINGS' HOLD DELAY) shows what it does with the other keys and knobs, for as long as it is held. Letting go then does nothing else.
  • The key that opens something closes it: a menu, a mode, an editor. EDIT opens an edit and leaves it keeping the changes; HOME leaves it dropping them (CHANGES DROPPED).

The knobs

  • SELECT moves the cursor up and down, ALGORITHM left and right. The cursor stops at the ends; only the instruments, the cartridges and the screens go round.
  • K1 to K4 change values at the cursor; the footer names what each turns. They never move the cursor.
  • Turned fast, a knob takes bigger steps (SETTINGS' KNOB SPEED); turned slowly, always one.
  • SEL + K1 (SEL held, any of K1-K4) takes big steps: an octave for a note, 10 for a value.

The keys and the current instrument

The keys play the current instrument on every screen, unless the screen gives them a job. The footer shows it on the left.

  • PRESETS picks the instrument, one a click, round within its cartridge (a cartridge is a bank of up to 128 instruments).
  • SEL + PRESETS (SEL held, or tapped first) turns the cartridges instead: the list of cartridges opens and each click picks the next. Let go of SEL (or touch another control) and PRESETS turns the instruments again.
  • OCT- and OCT+ shift the keys by an octave, from -4 to +4 (OCT +3).

The keys have no velocity: they play at SETTINGS' KEYS VOLUME. SETTINGS also sets the keys' default octave and how the effects treat them.

The arpeggiator

ARP switches the arpeggiator on and off on every screen but three: the EDITOR and LOOPS, where ARP has a job of its own, and DJ, where the keys are the decks'. While it is on, the keys you hold take turns as a rhythm instead of sounding together. Switched on with no key held, it waits for your first key.

  • The notes follow SETTINGS' ARP RHYTHM (a row a step), in the order of ARP PATTERN (UP, DOWN, UP-DOWN, RANDOM, AS PLAYED).
  • ARP LATCH keeps up to 1-8 notes playing after you let go of their keys; a key pressed with none held starts a new set. OFF: a note stops with its key.
  • Held, ARP changes them from the knobs: ARP + SELECT the rhythm, ARP + ALGORITHM the pattern (ARP UP), ARP + K1 the latch (LATCH 4 NOTES), ARP + LFO lets the latched notes go.
  • To stop latched notes and keep the arpeggiator on, tap ARP with no key held: the first tap lets the latched notes go, and ARP stays on; the next tap switches it off.
  • Changing screens switches it off.

Menus, questions and names

  • SEL opens the menu of what is at the cursor (copy, paste, move, delete ...), its last choice ready. SELECT picks, SEL (or the key that opened it) chooses, HOME closes. Only what can act is listed: REVERT, for example, only when there is something not saved.
  • Groups: an item marked > at the right holds more items (ROWS, TRANSFORM). SEL opens it; its first line, < BACK, goes back up; HOME closes the whole menu from any level.
  • MOVE: SELECT carries the thing, SEL puts it down, HOME puts it back.
  • Questions: the answers sit over their keys, in their own words (REVERT or KEEP, YES or NO): OCT+ on the right answers yes, OCT- on the left no; HOME cancels, and nothing happens. Nothing else acts while a question shows.
  • Typing a name: ALGORITHM moves along the name, SELECT changes the letter, SEL + SELECT jumps to the next group of characters (letters, digits, signs), LFO deletes a letter, OCT+ adds a space; EDIT is done, HOME cancels. Names take capitals, digits, the space and : . - ? | / \ * # $ @ %. An instrument's name holds 10 characters, a cartridge's 12, a song's 16; a name left empty becomes NO NAME.

The help on the FM-1

HOME + LFO, on any screen, opens LOOK FOR ONSWERS: a few pages on the screen you are on, then pages shared by all screens (the global keys, HOME, the screens, buttons, knobs, saving). SELECT turns the pages; HOME gets you back. In the help, keys are yellow, and a button whose print reads wrong gets its reading once: ENV (Explore Named Vaults), SEQ (Show Else, Quick), ARP (Again, Repeat, Please).

Keys on every screen

KeyDoes
KEYSThe keys play the current instrument, unless the screen gives them another job (on LOOPS' CONTROL mode, DJ and FX's LIVE page, for example).

PLAY REC KEYSThese act the moment you press them, for timing. Every other button acts when you let it go.

SAVE + OCT+Saves too: use it when you held SAVE so long that letting go no longer counts as a tap.

First steps

Half an hour with PT/FM: play a demo song, play the keys, write a pattern, record a loop, and save. The demo disk should be on the FM-1 (chapter 2).

Play a demo song

  1. Switch the FM-1 on. It starts on STATUS, which shows the version and how to get help.
  2. Press HOME + OP1: SONGS, the list of songs.
  3. Turn SELECT to a song, then press PLAY. Turn MASTER for the volume.
  4. Press PLAY again to pause; hold it to stop and go back to the start.
The FM-1's speaker plays one channel only, and PT/FM sends stereo at first, so a part panned to the other side is not heard on it. To hear the whole mix on the speaker, set SETTINGS' OUTPUT to MONO; set it back to STEREO for headphones. A cable in the output jack mutes the speaker.

Play the keys

  1. Play the keys: they play the current instrument, named in the footer's left corner.
  2. Turn PRESETS to try the instruments of its cartridge.
  3. Hold SEL and turn PRESETS to change the cartridge: try F8, the JUNO-106, or FA, the TB-303.
  4. Press OCT- or OCT+ to play lower or higher.

Write a pattern

  1. Press HOME + OP2: the EDITOR, with its own pattern. Tracks go across, rows go down; each row is a step in time.
  2. Press REC: its light comes on, and the keys now write.
  3. Play a key: the note is written at the cursor with the current instrument, and the cursor moves down. Play more. SELECT moves up and down, ALGORITHM to another track; LFO clears a cell.
  4. Press REC to stop writing, then PLAY: the pattern plays in a loop from the cursor's row. To hear it from the top, turn SELECT back to row 00 first.

The loop plays at the current song's tempo and through its effects: the song at the cursor on SONGS. To make it faster or slower, change that song's TEMPO (SONGS, GLO), or make the pattern a song of its own, as below.

The EDITOR's own pattern is a sketch pad. To use it in a song, give it a number: SEL, STORE IN A PATTERN (chapter 7).

Make it a song

A song is a list of patterns played one after another, its order. From the pattern you wrote to a song of your own:

  1. In the EDITOR, press SEL and pick STORE IN A PATTERN, then + NEW PATTERN: your pattern gets the first free number (STORED IN PATTERN 00), and the EDITOR follows it there.
  2. Press HOME + OP1 for SONGS. Press SEL and pick NEW: the pattern list asks what the song starts with (NEW SONG STARTS WITH). Turn SELECT to your pattern and press SEL. The song, NEW SONG, is added at the end of the list and becomes the current song.
  3. Press EDIT to go into its order. SEL opens the position's menu: CLONE PATTERN puts a copy of the pattern after it, to vary; NEW PATTERN puts an empty one after it. K1 changes which pattern a position plays, and EDIT PATTERN in the menu opens it in the EDITOR (HOME comes back). Press EDIT again when the order is done.
  4. Press GLO for the song's properties: set its TEMPO with K1 (the BPM it makes is shown beside it), give it a NAME (EDIT types it), and choose whether it loops or stops AT THE END. GLO closes.
  5. Press PLAY to hear the whole song, then SAVE.

Record a loop

  1. Press HOME + POLY: LOOPS. The cursor is on + NEW LOOP.
  2. Pick a sound with PRESETS, then press REC.
  3. Play: recording starts with your first note (or press PLAY to start it on the beat).
  4. Press REC again: the loop closes at the next bar line and plays on. Its length is now every loop's length.
  5. Pick another sound and press REC again: the next loop starts with the loops' next round.

Save

Everything you did is in the FM-1's working memory: the SAVE light is dim. Press SAVE. When the music plays, the save waits for a pause; press PLAY to pause and it is written: SAVED. Now your pattern and loops survive switching off.

SONGS

SONGS lists every song, and below the list shows the picked song's order: the patterns it plays, one after another. The song at the cursor is the current song everywhere: PLAY plays it, and the EDITOR opens on its patterns. Open it with HOME + OP1.

The list

  • SELECT picks a song: it becomes the current song.
  • PLAY plays it, from the boxed position; again, pauses. The playing song has a play mark and its name turns green.
  • ALGORITHM moves the box: the position PLAY will start from (PLAY FROM POS 03 in the header). While the song plays, only the box moves; it waits for the next PLAY.
  • The header counts the songs (3/18); the footer's right side shows the current song's BPM and length.
  • A position whose pattern is missing shows its number in red.

When a song ends: the play modes

SEQ turns the play mode round (ONE PLAY, REPEAT SONG, PLAY NEXT). It decides how a song started here ends, if the song itself stops at its end:

  • ONE PLAY (at first): it stops.
  • REPEAT SONG: it plays again from its start.
  • PLAY NEXT: the next song in the list plays at once, and the cursor follows it; after the last song, playing stops.

A song set to loop (AT THE END: LOOP) loops in every mode. The mode holds on every screen until something else plays (a pattern in the EDITOR, LOOPS, DJ), and it is not saved.

Changing a song's order

Press EDIT on a song: the cursor moves into its order, onto the boxed position, and EDIT lights.

  • SELECT moves a line (8 positions) up or down, ALGORITHM one position left or right.
  • K1 puts another pattern at the position (K1 PATTERN 0A); with SEL held, 8 at a time.
  • LFO removes the position.
  • ENV opens the pattern list; ENV again puts the highlighted pattern at the position.
  • SEL opens the position's menu (below).
  • EDIT leaves the order keeping the changes; HOME leaves dropping them (CHANGES DROPPED): a pattern made meanwhile is deleted again.
EDIT PATTERN
Opens the position's pattern in the EDITOR; HOME comes back here.
NEW PATTERN
An empty pattern at the first free number, put in after the position (PATTERN 0C MADE).
INSERT
A position before the cursor's, with the same pattern.
DELETE
Removes the position, as LFO does.
COPY, PASTE
COPY takes the position's pattern number (PATTERN 03 COPIED); PASTE puts it in after the position.
CLONE PATTERN
Copies the position's pattern to a new number and uses the copy here (03 CLONED TO 0C), so you can change it without changing the other places that play the original.
REVERT
The song as last saved (listed only while it has unsaved changes).

Your patterns are numbered 00 to EF (240 of them). With all used, NEW PATTERN and CLONE PATTERN say NO FREE PATTERN.

The song menu

SEL on the list opens the song's menu:

NEW
A new song. First pick the pattern it starts with from the list (NEW SONG STARTS WITH), or + NEW PATTERN for an empty one; HOME makes nothing. The song, NEW SONG, is added at the end of the list (tempo 120, LOOP). Past song FD: NO FREE SONG NUMBER.
CLONE
A copy of the song, after it, named with " 2".
MOVE
Another place in the list: SELECT carries it, SEL puts it down (SONG MOVED TO 02), HOME takes it back (NOT MOVED).
DELETE
Asks first (DELETE SONG 00?). The line ITS PATTERNS TOO is ticked at first: the song's own patterns, those no other song and no FUSION instrument uses, are deleted with it (SONG 00 DELETED, 4 PATTERNS TOO), and the line says how many there are and how much room they free. To keep them, clear the tick with K1. Patterns other songs use always stay. OCT+ deletes, OCT- keeps the song, HOME cancels.
RENAME
Type its name (up to 16 characters); EDIT is done.
UNLOAD SONG
Once a song, the EDITOR's pattern loop, the loops or DJ's decks have played, the keys go on sounding through that one's effects and tempo, even after it stops (chapter 15). UNLOAD SONG stops everything at once, forgets the song's place, and gives the keys back their own effects and tempo, THE KEYS', as at power-on (SONG UNLOADED). The loops and DJ's stand stay as they are. It is listed only when there is something to unload; PLAY afterwards plays the current song from its start.
REVERT
The song as last saved: its order, name, properties, mixer and effects (not its patterns), after a question (REVERT SONG 00 TO SAVED?).

ENV on the list opens the pattern list; the pattern picked becomes the EDITOR's (PATTERN 0A FOR THE EDITOR); PLAY in the list hears the highlighted pattern.

A song's properties

GLO opens the song's properties. SELECT picks one, K1 changes it at once (SEL held: TEMPO by 10, SWING by 5), EDIT on NAME types it; GLO or HOME closes.

How time works in a song: each row lasts a number of ticks (TICKS A ROW), and TEMPO sets how fast the ticks go (a tick lasts 2.5 seconds divided by TEMPO). Leave TICKS A ROW at 6 and ROWS A BEAT at 4, as a new song has them, and TEMPO is the BPM: for 128 BPM, set TEMPO to 80 (hex for 128). Whatever the three are, the screen shows the BPM they make.

NAME
Up to 16 characters.
TEMPO
How fast the song plays, with the BPM it makes: 8C (140 BPM). 3-600 (hex 03-258)
TICKS A ROW
The ticks in a row: commands that act during a row (slides, arpeggios, retriggers) act on each tick. 1-31
ROWS A BEAT
How many rows make a beat. Besides the BPM, it decides which row numbers the EDITOR colours as beats and bars, and how many rows DJ counts as a beat. 1-16
SWING
Every second row played late. 50-75 %
AT THE END
What the song does after its last position. LOOP, STOP
LOOP FROM
The position a looping song goes back to. POSITION 00 to the last

The BPM is TEMPO × 24 / (TICKS A ROW × ROWS A BEAT), rounded: a song at TEMPO 140, 6 ticks a row, 4 rows a beat plays at 140 BPM.

Keys on SONGS

KeyOn the list
SELECTPick a song. In the order: a line (8 positions) up / down.
ALGORITHMWhere PLAY starts (the box). In the order: a position left / right.
SELECT ALGORITHMIn the order: move through the positions, a line or one at a time.
PLAYPlay / pause the song; in the pattern list, hear the highlighted pattern.
EDITInto the song's order; in the order, done, keeping the changes.
GLOThe song's properties: name, tempo, swing, loop or stop.
SEQThe play mode: ONE PLAY, REPEAT SONG, PLAY NEXT.
SELThe song's menu; in the order, the position's menu.
ENVThe pattern list (for the EDITOR); in the order, again puts the highlighted pattern at the position.
K1In the order: another pattern at the position.
LFOIn the order: remove the position.
HOMEIn the order: leave it, dropping the changes.
KEYS OCT- OCT+ PRESETSPlay, as on every screen.
ARPThe arpeggiator on / off.
KEYS heldWith ARP on, the notes held take turns.
ARP heldWith SELECT, ALGORITHM, K1: the rhythm, the order, the latch.

EDITOR

The EDITOR writes patterns: a grid of tracks across and rows down. Each cell holds a note, the instrument that plays it, a volume and up to four commands. Open it with HOME + OP2.

The grid

  • SELECT moves up and down the rows, ALGORITHM across the tracks. Nothing wraps; past the last row of a page the next page shows.
  • SEQ turns the view: 8, 4, 2 or 1 tracks at once (8 TRACKS ... 1 TRACK). Fewer tracks show more of each cell: 8 tracks the notes only, 4 the instrument too, 2 a command as well, 1 the whole cell with all four commands.
  • Row numbers are hexadecimal, 00 to 7F. Beat rows are cyan, each bar's first row light cyan. When this pattern plays, the playing row sits on a blue band; the view stays with the cursor.
  • In a cell, --- is no note, === a note off, .. no volume (the instrument's own) and ..:.. no instrument (the track's plays on).
  • The footer's right side says the command (or volume) under the cursor in words: A04 VOLUME -4.

Which pattern you edit

The EDITOR edits one pattern at a time: its own, or a numbered one.

  • Its own pattern (the header says just EDITOR): a sketch pad no song can play. SAVE keeps it after switching off. A fresh FM-1 opens on it.
  • A numbered pattern (EDITOR 12): your edits go straight into pattern 12, and every song that plays it hears them.

From the cell's SEL menu (nothing marked):

NEW PATTERN
Empties the EDITOR's own pattern (8 tracks × 64 rows) and opens it.
LOAD A PATTERN
Copies a numbered pattern into the EDITOR's own, to start from it (PATTERN 1A LOADED). The numbered one is not changed.
STORE IN A PATTERN
Gives what the EDITOR shows a number, so songs can play it: pick a pattern, or + NEW PATTERN for the first free number (STORED IN PATTERN 1A); the EDITOR follows it there. Storing over a pattern that holds anything asks first (PATTERN 0C WILL BE REPLACED, DO YOU WANT TO CONTINUE?).
Opening another pattern empties the EDITOR's own. When it holds anything, a question asks first: EDITOR CHANGES WILL BE LOST, DO YOU WANT TO CONTINUE?. Store it in a pattern first if you want to keep it.

The pattern list: ENV opens it (PATTERNS: number, size, a map of notes by track, the songs using it; unused patterns dim). ENV again opens the highlighted pattern; PLAY hears it on its own, looped, and what played before pauses, keeping its place. Moving the highlight moves the preview; PLAY again stops it (ARP does what PLAY does here). Picking a pattern or leaving the list ends the preview, and the next PLAY resumes what played before. HOME closes. Its SEL menu:

NEW
An empty pattern, 8 tracks × 64 rows, at the first free number (PATTERN 13 MADE); with all 240 used, ALL 240 PATTERNS USED.
CLONE
A copy of the highlighted pattern at the first free number (12 CLONED TO 13).
MOVE
To another free number: SELECT carries it, SEL puts it down (PATTERN 12 MOVED TO 20); with none free, NO FREE NUMBER. Songs using it ask to follow (references).
DELETE
Deletes it (PATTERN 12 DELETED), asking first when something uses it.

Writing notes

REC switches writing. With REC off (REC OFF: KEYS PLAY) the keys only play the current instrument, so you can try sounds freely. With REC on (REC ON: KEYS WRITE, REC lit), the keys write:

  1. Pick the sound with PRESETS: the note is written with the current instrument and SETTINGS' KEYS VOLUME.
  2. Play a key: its note is written at the cursor and sounds; the cell's commands stay.
  3. The cursor moves down by the edit step (GLO's EDIT STEP; 0 stays put). Keys pressed together (a chord) land on the same row, spreading to the next tracks.
  • LFO clears the cell and moves on; on an empty cell it writes a note off (===).
  • REC while a song plays pauses the song (SONG PAUSED: WRITING).
  • REC while the EDITOR's loop plays: the loop plays on and the keys write step by step at the cursor; it plays what you write as it reaches it. PLAY then pauses the loop (LOOP STOPPED: PLAY FOR A TAKE), and the next PLAY starts a take.
  • Every change is heard at once by whatever plays this pattern (the EDITOR's loop, a song, a DJ deck).
  • K1-K4, LFO, the menu and the note editor change cells whether REC is on or off.
  • A note written with no instrument (..:..) plays the track's last instrument.
  • To change the sound of notes already written, change each cell's INSTR in the note editor (below); there is no change for many cells at once. On LOOPS, APPLY INSTRUMENT gives a whole loop another sound.

PLAY with REC off plays the pattern in a loop from the cursor's row.

Volume and commands: K1 to K4

The knobs change the cell at the cursor, without moving the cursor:

K1
Picks which part of the cell the other knobs change: the volume, or command 1 to 4 (one past the last, to add one) (K1 VOLUME, K1 CMD 1 ACCENT). The grid shows the command in that place.
K2
The command there, through every command there is (below); back to NO COMMAND removes it.
K3, K4
Its value, a digit each. On the volume, K3 steps by 16 and K4 by 1. For an instrument parameter (*), mixer value (=) or FX knob (#), K3 picks which and K4 sets it. SEL held: K4 by 16.

The volume runs from 00 (silent) to 7F, the instrument at its full level. Turned past 7F it becomes .., no volume: the note plays at the instrument's own default (for a sampler instrument, its VOLUME). The VOLUME command (Cxx) uses the trackers' smaller scale, 00 to 40, where 40 is as loud as a volume of 7F.

An example: to fade a note out, put the cursor on it, turn K1 to CMD 1, K2 to VOL SLIDE (Axy), and K4 to 4: the cell shows A04, and the note's volume falls by 4 on every tick of the row. The footer says what the command at the cursor does, in words.

The note editor

EDIT on a cell opens it as a list of fields, a line each: NOTE, INSTR (its sound), VOLUME, CMD 1 to CMD 4, and + COMMAND to add one.

  • SELECT moves a line up or down, ALGORITHM across a command line (the command, its value).
  • K1 changes the part at the cursor a step; K2 in big steps: an octave, a cartridge, 16, or the next group of commands (each command is explained below).
  • SEL makes SELECT and ALGORITHM move to the neighbouring cells instead (SELECT, ALG: CELLS), without leaving; SEL again goes back to the fields (SELECT, ALG: FIELDS).
  • The KEYS change the note; LFO clears the cell.
  • EDIT closes it keeping the changes; HOME drops them.

Recording live: takes

With REC on and nothing playing, PLAY records a take: from the cursor's row round and round the pattern, adding on each pass, until PLAY or REC stops it.

  1. Press PLAY: recording starts as you let go, after SETTINGS' COUNT-IN (1 or 2 bars of clicks, or none). With COUNT-IN set to KEY, your first note starts it.
  2. Or hold PLAY and press a key: the take starts on that note at once. Hold PLAY alone to see both ways (LET GO: START THE TAKE, PRESS A KEY: START ON THAT NOTE).
  3. Play. Notes land on SETTINGS' QUANTIZE grid (2, 3 or 4 rows, a row, or REAL TIME); letting go of a key writes a note off. A melody stays on the cursor's track; a chord spreads to the next tracks.
  4. Press PLAY or REC to stop (TAKE STOPPED). REC stays on and the cursor goes back to the row the take started on.

During a count-in a box in the middle of the screen counts it: COUNT-IN, the beats left in big figures, and the bar (BAR 1 OF 2). With COUNT-IN set to KEY, the box says TAKE ARMED, PLAY A NOTE, until your first note.

REC blinks during a take and its count-in. An armed take is cancelled with HOME, PLAY or REC (TAKE CANCELLED). A full edit memory ends a take, keeping what was written.

Listening to a row

ARP on the EDITOR repeats the cursor's row at the song's tempo, in SETTINGS' ARP RHYTHM (ROW PREVIEW #___; again, ROW PREVIEW OFF). Whatever plays stops first, so the row is heard alone; moving the cursor moves the preview. ARP + SELECT changes the rhythm (RHYTHM ##_: # plays a row, _ rests one).

Blocks

  1. SEL, MARK: then SELECT and ALGORITHM stretch a block over rows and tracks from the cursor. Or hold SEL and turn them.
  2. SEL again opens the block's menu.
COPY, CUT, PASTE
Through a clipboard kept until power-off (COPIED 4 X 1: rows × tracks). Over 2 KB: BLOCK TOO BIG TO COPY; an empty clipboard: NOTHING COPIED.
PASTE MIX
Pastes into empty cells only.
CLEAR
Empties the block.
MOVE, SWAP
Carry the block with the cursor; SEL puts it down. MOVE leaves its old place empty, SWAP puts what was there in its place; HOME cancels (CANCELLED).
INSERT ROW, DELETE ROW
Under ROWS. INSERT ROW puts an empty row at the cursor's row, the rows below moving down (the pattern's last row is lost); DELETE ROW takes the cursor's row out, the rows below moving up. With a block marked, it acts on the block's tracks; with nothing marked, on the cursor's track and every track to its right, so from the first track it is every track.
TRANSPOSE
Under TRANSFORM: K1 a semitone, SEL held an octave, SEL ends it (TRANSPOSED +02).
INTERPOLATE
Under TRANSFORM: a sweep. A command on the block's first and last rows goes on every row between, its value stepping from one to the other; without one, the volumes step.

The pipette: SEL, TAKE ITS INSTRUMENT, or ENV held: the cursor's cell's instrument becomes the current one (the toast names it, 01:05 EL PIANO DX7); none there: NO INSTRUMENT HERE.

RECORD PATTERN: steps on the white keys

SEL, RECORD PATTERN opens a step sequencer: the white keys switch 16 steps on and off, and REC writes their notes into the cursor's track from the cursor's row (PATTERN: 12 NOTES). It is the same recorder LOOPS has; LOOPS explains its keys. Here K4 picks TO THE END (the steps repeated down to the pattern's last row) or ONCE. Nothing already there is removed: a step off leaves its cell as it is.

The pattern's properties

GLO opens the pattern's properties: SELECT picks one, K1 changes it, GLO or HOME closes them.

TRACKS
1-16
ROWS
SEL held: by 16. 1-128
EDIT STEP
How far the cursor moves after a note. 0-16
USED BY
The songs that play it, and FUSION when a FUSION instrument does; not changeable.

Making the pattern smaller where notes would go asks first (THIS DROPS 12 CELLS, MAKE THE PATTERN SMALLER?).

The commands

A cell holds up to four commands, acting in their order. Each takes 3 characters in the grid: the command, then its value. Values are hexadecimal; x and y are one digit (0-F), xx two (00-FF).

Rows and ticks. Every row is cut into ticks: TICKS A ROW in the song's properties, 6 at first. A command works either once, as the row starts (the "fine" ones, a volume, a pan), or on every tick after the first (slides, vibratos, volume slides move a little each tick, so the same command is stronger with more ticks a row). In the slides, vibratos and volume slides, a value of 00 goes on with the last one that track used.

K2 turns through the commands in this order: the tracker effects (0-9, then A-Z), the volume-column ones (~), PT/FM's own, then *, = and #. Below they are grouped by what they change.

Pitch

GridNameDoes
0xyARPEGGIOPlays the note, the note x semitones up and the note y semitones up in turn, a tick each, over and over for the row: a chord from one voice, the chip-music arpeggio. 037 is a minor chord, 047 a major one.
1xx, 2xxSLIDE UP, SLIDE DOWNThe pitch slides up (or down) by xx sixteenths of a semitone every tick: 10 slides a semitone a tick. It keeps the new pitch until the next note.
3xxSLIDE TO NOTEPortamento: the cell's note is not started; instead the note playing glides toward it at speed xx (sixteenths of a semitone a tick) and stops there. Put 300 on the following rows to keep gliding.
4xyVIBRATOThe pitch wobbles around the note: x is how fast, y how deep. 400 goes on with the last speed and depth.
5xySLIDE TO NOTE + VOLGoes on gliding to the note as 300 does, and slides the volume as Axy does.
6xyVIBRATO + VOLGoes on with the vibrato as 400 does, and slides the volume as Axy does.
E1x, E2xFINE SLIDE UP, DOWNMoves the pitch up (or down) by x sixteenths of a semitone, once, as the row starts: a small correction rather than a slide.
X1x, X2xEXTRA FINE UP, DOWNAs E1x and E2x, four times finer.
E3xGLISSANDOE31 makes slides to a note (3xx, 5xy, ~Mx) heard in semitone steps, as a glissando on a keyboard; E30 makes them smooth again.
E4xVIBRATO WAVEThe shape of the vibrato's wobble: 0 sine, 1 saw, 2 square, 3 random.
E5xFINETUNETunes the note as it starts, by x - 8 eighths of a semitone: E50 is a semitone flat, E58 in tune, E5F nearly a semitone sharp.
UxyFINE VIBRATOAs 4xy, four times shallower: a gentle shimmer.
~Sx, ~VxVIBRATO SPEED, DEPTHThe volume column's vibrato: ~Sx sets its speed, ~Vx vibrates with depth x.
~MxSLIDE TO NOTEThe volume column's 3xx, at speed x × 16.

Volume

GridNameDoes
CxxVOLUMESets the note's volume on the trackers' scale, 00 (silent) to 40 (full, the same as a cell volume of 7F).
AxyVOLUME SLIDEThe volume rises by x every tick (Ax0), or falls by y (A0y): a fade in or out within the row. AxF and AFy are fine slides: once, as the row starts.
EAx, EBxFINE VOLUME UP, DOWNRaises (or lowers) the volume by x, once, as the row starts.
7xyTREMOLOThe volume wobbles: x is how fast, y how deep.
E7xTREMOLO WAVEThe shape of the tremolo: 0 sine, 1 saw, 2 square, 3 random.
TxyTREMORThe note sounds for x ticks and is silent for y ticks, again and again: a hard, rhythmic chop. A 0 keeps the last value.
GxxGLOBAL VOLUMEThe whole song's volume, 00 to 40 (full), from any track.
HxyGLOBAL VOL SLIDEThe whole song's volume rises by x (or falls by y) every tick: a fade of the whole song.
~-x, ~+xVOL SLIDE DOWN, UPThe volume column's volume slide: down (or up) by x every tick.
~Dx, ~UxFINE VOL DOWN, UPDown (or up) by x, once, as the row starts.

Pan

GridNameDoes
8xxPANPlaces the track: 00 fully left, 80 in the middle, FF fully right. It is the track's pan, the same as the MIXER's PAN.
PxyPAN SLIDEThe pan moves right by x (or left by y) every tick.
YxyPANBRELLOThe pan swings around its place, left and right: x is how fast, y how wide.
~PxPANThe volume column's pan: 0 left, 8 the middle, F right.
~<x, ~>xPAN SLIDE LEFT, RIGHTThe pan moves left (or right) by x every tick.

Notes and timing

GridNameDoes
EDxNOTE DELAYThe note starts x ticks into the row instead of on it: a flam, a late hit, a swing feel on one note.
ECxNOTE CUTThe note is silenced at tick x of the row: short, staccato notes.
KxxKEY OFFLets the note go at tick xx, as a key released: it fades by its own release instead of stopping dead.
E9xRETRIGGERStarts the note again every x ticks: a drum roll from one hit.
RxyMULTI RETRIGGERStarts the note again every y ticks, changing the volume each time by x: 1 to 5 lower it by 1, 2, 4, 8, 16; 6 makes it 2/3 and 7 half; 9 to D raise it by 1, 2, 4, 8, 16; E makes it 1.5 times, F twice; 0 and 8 leave it. A roll that fades or builds.
9xxSAMPLE OFFSETSampler instruments: the sample starts xx × 256 samples in, from its START, so a long sample can be started in its middle.
LEGLEGATOOn a note: the note the track still holds moves to this one with no new attack, its envelope going on. Only with the same instrument; a TB-303 needs SLD on the note before; a FUSION instrument always starts a new note.
ACCACCENTTB-303: the note accented, louder and with its filter opening further, as the 303's accent.
SLDSLIDETB-303: this note glides into the next one, with no new attack, as the 303's slide.
A+SACCENT + SLIDEBoth on one note, in one place.

The song's flow and tempo (from any track)

GridNameDoes
FxxTICKS / TEMPOF01 to F1F: that many ticks a row (fewer is faster, the tick staying as it is). F20 to FFF: the TEMPO (a tick's length; at 6 ticks and 4 rows a beat, the BPM). F00: back to the song's own TEMPO and ticks.
BxxJUMPAfter this row, the song goes on at its position xx.
DxxBREAKAfter this row, the song goes on at the next position, from its row xx (D00 from the start): a pattern cut short.
E6xLOOPE60 marks a row; a later E6x (x 1-F) goes back to the mark x more times: a few rows repeated without copying them.
EExPATTERN DELAYHolds this row x rows longer, its notes not played again: a pause in the pattern.

PT/FM's own

GridNameDoes
*xxPARAMETERTurns a knob of the track's instrument, as on its edit page (a JUNO-106's VCF FREQ, a DX7's OP2 LEVEL, a TB-303's CUTOFF ...): K3 picks which, K4 sets it. The sound keeps it until changed, so a row of them turns the knob over time; another instrument on the track drops it.
=xxMIXERSets the track's place in the mixer: K3 picks LEVEL, CHORUS SEND, DELAY SEND, REVERB SEND or DUCK AMOUNT, K4 the value.
#xxFXTurns any knob of the song's effects (K3 picks it, K4 sets it), or switches an effect on or off. It holds until the next song starts.
!xxLOOP 1/4 ... VINYL STOPA punch-in effect, as if its key were held for xx rows (!08: 8 rows), so a song can carry its own loops, sweeps and stops (FX).
  • B, D, E6, EE, F, G, H, # and ! act on the whole song, from any track. In a FUSION pattern they are ignored, shown dim.
  • A command for what you are editing right now (an effect on FX, the mixer, an instrument's edit page, a song's properties) is skipped while you edit it, so nothing jumps under your hands.
  • EDIT (the note editor) says each command in words.

Keys on the EDITOR

KeyDoes
SELECTUp / down the rows; in the note editor, a line.
ALGORITHMAcross the tracks; in the note editor, a command or its value.
SEQ8, 4, 2 or 1 tracks at once.
PRESETSThe sound the keys write.
KEYSREC off: play. REC on: write at the cursor. In the note editor: change the note.
RECWriting on / off. While the loop plays, it plays on and the keys write at the cursor.
PLAYREC off: loop the pattern from the cursor's row. REC on: record a take (starts as you let go); stop the loop, then PLAY for a take; during a take, stop it.
PLAY held + KEYSREC on: start a take on that note. PLAY held alone shows how.
PLAY RECDuring a take: stop recording.
KEYS heldIn a take, a note lasts as long as its key is held: letting go writes a note off.
K1The slot: volume or command 1-4. In the note editor: change the part at the cursor.
K2The command (slide, accent ...). In the note editor: big steps.
K3 K4Its two digits, or the volume; in *, = and #, K3 picks which, K4 sets it.
K1 K2 K3 K4Never move the cursor.
LFOClear the cell (and move on); on an empty cell, a note off.
EDITThe note editor; in it, done (it says each command in words).
HOMEClose what is open (the note editor dropping its changes, a carried block, a mark); entered from another screen, back there.
GLOThe pattern's properties: tracks, rows, edit step.
ENVThe pattern list; again, open the one picked; in it, PLAY hears one.
ENV heldThe pipette: take the cursor's sound.
SELThe menu: MARK, TAKE ITS INSTRUMENT, the block's menu, NEW / LOAD / STORE A PATTERN, RECORD PATTERN, REVERT. In the note editor: move to other cells, again back. In the list: NEW, CLONE, MOVE, DELETE.
SEL held + SELECT SEL held + ALGORITHMMark a block: with SEL held, SELECT stretches it over rows, ALGORITHM over tracks.
ARPRepeat the cursor's row (the row preview).
ARP heldWith SELECT: the preview's rhythm.
SAVEKeeps the EDITOR's own pattern after switching off.
white keysIn RECORD PATTERN: the steps.
HOME + white keyMute a track; held, or after SEQ, solo.

INSTRUMENTS

INSTRUMENTS picks, plays and edits the sounds. Sounds live in cartridges: a cartridge is a bank of up to 128 instruments of one type, each in a numbered slot (01:05 is cartridge 01, slot 05). Open it with HOME + OP3.

Browsing and playing

  • The cursor is the current instrument: SELECT moves a slot at a time, ALGORITHM by 8 (a column).
  • PRESETS steps to the next or previous sound there is, skipping empty slots, round.
  • K1 turns the cartridges, round.
  • The KEYS play the sound picked; ARP arpeggiates it, so with ARP LATCH both hands are free for the knobs.
  • The bottom half shows the sound: a DX7's operators, a JUNO-106's sliders, a TB-303's knobs, a CHIP sound's steps and tables, a sample's waveform, a FUSION's pattern as a little map.
  • GLO shows the cartridge's name, type and slots used, and renames it.
  • ENV lists all the cartridges (CARTRIDGES: ID, name, type, slots used); ENV again opens the highlighted one.

Changing a sound: edit mode

Press EDIT: the list gives way to the sound's settings below and a picture of it above (the DX7's algorithm and envelope, the JUNO-106's envelope and filter, the sample's waveform ...).

  • The settings are a table, four to a row (a group). SELECT picks a row; K1 to K4 change its four values (RELEASE 33 MS in the header as you turn).
  • ALGORITHM or SEQ turn the pages of settings (SEQ goes round).
  • The KEYS play the sound as it changes; every change is heard at once, by everything that plays it.
  • LFO puts the knob turned last back to its default (LEVEL 0 DB (DEFAULT)).
  • PRESETS moves to another sound, still editing.
  • SEL on NAME types the name; elsewhere it opens the menu: COPY, PASTE, INIT, RENAME, AUTO LEVEL, REVERT (FUSION: EDIT PATTERN too).
  • SEL held + a knob: big steps (LEVEL by 6 dB, a value by 10).
  • EDIT leaves, keeping the changes; HOME leaves, dropping them (CHANGES DROPPED).

An empty slot has nothing to edit: EMPTY SLOT: SEL, INIT (except FUSION, below).

LEVEL
Every instrument has one: how loud it is, in dB, half a dB a click. AUTO LEVEL (in the SEL menu) measures the sound and sets it as loud as the others (LEVEL SET TO -1.5 DB; a silent sound: NO SOUND TO MEASURE). -64 to +63.5 dB
NAME
The sound's name; SEL on it types it.

DX7

The DX7 makes sound by FM: six sine-wave operators, each with its own envelope. Some (the carriers) are heard; the others (the modulators) bend their waves, which gives bells, electric pianos, basses and brass. Its four pages:

OPERATORS
The first page: a row for each operator.
OP1, OP2, OP3, OP4, OP5, OP6
The six rows, one an operator. Each has the same four knobs:
LEVEL
K1: how loud the operator is (a carrier), or how strongly it bends the others (a modulator). 0-99
COARSE
K2: the operator's frequency as a multiple of the note's: 1 is the note, 2 an octave up, 3 an octave and a fifth; 0 is half. Whole multiples sound harmonic, the others bell-like. 0-31
FINE
K3: adds to COARSE in small steps, up to almost twice its multiple. 0-99
DETUNE
K4: a slight detune, for a slow beating between operators. -7 to +7
ENVELOPES
Two rows for each operator: how its volume moves over a note.
OP1 RATE, OP2 RATE, OP3 RATE, OP4 RATE, OP5 RATE, OP6 RATE
An operator's four rates, R1 to R4 on K1 to K4.
OP1 LVL, OP2 LVL, OP3 LVL, OP4 LVL, OP5 LVL, OP6 LVL
Its four levels, L1 to L4 on K1 to K4.
R1, R2, R3, R4
How fast the envelope moves to each level: R1 to L1, R2 to L2, R3 to L3, and, once the key is let go, R4 to L4. 99 is the fastest, 0 the slowest. 0-99
L1, L2, L3, L4
The levels it moves to: it rises to L1, goes on to L2, then to L3, where it stays while the key is held; let go, it moves to L4 (usually 0: silence). 0-99
PITCH / LFO
The pitch envelope and the LFO.
P RATE, P LEVEL
The pitch envelope: its rates R1-R4 and levels L1-L4 move as an operator's envelope does, but on the pitch of the whole voice. Level 50 is the note's own pitch; above it bends up, below it down. 0-99
LFO
The LFO's first row. The LFO is a slow wave that moves the pitch or the volume:
SPEED
K1: how fast the LFO's wave goes. 0-99
DELAY
K2: how long after the key the LFO fades in. 0-99
PM DEPTH
K3: how much it moves the pitch: vibrato. 0-99
AM DEPTH
K4: how much it moves the volume: tremolo, on the operators whose stored sensitivity lets it (below). 0-99
LFO 2
The LFO's second row:
WAVE
K1: the LFO's wave; S+H is random steps. TRI, SAW-, SAW+, SQR, SINE, S+H
SYNC
K2: ON, the LFO starts again with each key; OFF, it runs on freely. OFF, ON
P SENS
K3: how strongly PM DEPTH acts on the pitch. 0-7
VOICE
The last page: NAME, LEVEL, and the row VOICE.
ALGORITHM
K1: which of the 32 ways the six operators are wired, which are heard and which modulate which; the picture shows it. 00-1F
FEEDBACK
K2: the loop drawn in the algorithm's picture, an operator modulating itself: brighter, then noisy. 0-7
OSC SYNC
K3: ON, every operator's wave starts again from zero with each key, so every note starts alike. OFF, ON
TRANSPOSE
K4: shifts the whole voice, in semitones. -24 to +24

A DX7 voice also stores what its pages do not show: keyboard scaling (louder or softer towards the ends of the keyboard), the sensitivities to velocity and to the LFO's AM, and fixed frequencies. Voices from DX7 cartridge files keep them, and PT/FM plays them as they are.

JUNO-106

The JUNO-106 is an analogue polysynth: one oscillator (DCO) with a pulse, a saw, a sub-oscillator and noise, through a resonant low-pass filter (VCF) and a high-pass, shaped by one envelope, with a chorus. Browsing, its sound shows as the original's sliders.

Its pages:

DCO
The first page, the oscillator. Its first row is named DCO too:
LFO
K1: vibrato, how much the LFO moves the pitch. 0-127
PWM
K2: the pulse's width: how far the LFO moves it (PWM BY LFO), or where it stands (PWM BY MAN). 0-127
NOISE
K3: how much noise is mixed in. 0-127
SUB
K4: the sub-oscillator, a square an octave down, mixed in. 0-127
WAVES
The second row:
RANGE
K1: the octave, 16' the lowest. 16', 8', 4'
PULSE
K2: the pulse wave on or off. OFF, ON
SAW
K3: the saw wave on or off; the two can sound together. OFF, ON
PWM BY
K4: LFO, the LFO moves the pulse's width; MAN, PWM sets a fixed width. LFO, MAN
FILTERS
The page of the filters.
VCF
The low-pass filter's row:
FREQ
K1: the cutoff: how bright the sound is. 0-127
RES
K2: resonance, a peak at the cutoff; turned high, the filter whistles. 0-127
ENV
K3: how far the envelope moves the cutoff over a note. 0-127
LFO
K4: how far the LFO sweeps the cutoff. 0-127
VCF 2
The second row:
KYBD
K1: how much the cutoff follows the note: higher notes brighter. 0-127
ENV +/-
K2: +, the envelope opens the filter; -, it closes it. +, -
HPF
K3: the high-pass filter: 0 boosts the bass, 1 leaves it flat, 2 and 3 make the sound thinner. 0-3
ENVELOPE
The page of the envelope, the amplifier and the LFO.
ENV
The envelope's row. The envelope shapes the volume (with MODE at ENV) and the filter (by VCF's ENV):
A
K1: attack, how fast the sound rises. 0-127
D
K2: decay, how fast it falls to the sustain level. 0-127
S
K3: sustain, the level it holds while the key is down. 0-127
R
K4: release, how long it fades once the key is let go. 0-127
VCA
The amplifier's row:
LEVEL
K1: the amplifier's level, before the instrument's own LEVEL in dB. 0-127
MODE
K2: ENV, the volume follows the envelope; GATE, full while the key is held, silent at once when let go. ENV, GATE
CHORUS
K3: the JUNO's own chorus, II the deeper. OFF, I, II
LFO
The LFO's row: the slow wave that DCO's LFO and PWM and VCF's LFO use.
RATE
K1: the LFO's speed. 0-127
DELAY
K2: how long after the key the LFO fades in. 0-127
VOICE
The last page: NAME and LEVEL.

TB-303

The TB-303 is the acid bass line: one oscillator through a squelchy resonant filter. In a pattern, the commands ACC (accent) and SLD (slide) play its two famous tricks (EDITOR). One page:

KNOBS
The page, and its first row, the original's knobs:
WAVE
K1: the oscillator's wave: saw at 0, square at 127, the two mixed between. 0-127
CUTOFF
K2: the filter's cutoff: how bright the sound is. 0-127
RESO
K3: resonance, the squelch: a peak at the cutoff. 0-127
ENV MOD
K4: how far each note's envelope opens the filter. 0-127
KNOBS 2
The second row:
DECAY
K1: how fast the filter closes again after each note. 0-127
ACCENT
K2: how much an accented note stands out: louder, brighter, a sharper sweep. 0-127

CHIP

CHIP is a virtual sound chip: it makes the sounds of 8-bit computers and consoles the way their chips made them, square waves at a few widths, a stepped triangle, a drawn wave, noise, 16 volume steps moving 50 or 60 times a second. Its four families: BRK (the handheld), 8BIT (the console), PSG (the computers' programmable sound generator) and 16BIT (that chip's finer later version). Any part works on any voice.

Its pages:

TONE
The first page: the oscillator, the noise, the clock and the sweep.
OSC
The oscillator's row. K1 picks the oscillator: PULSE, TRIANGLE, WAVE (one of 16 drawn waves), BUZZ (the PSG's envelope run fast enough to be a tone) or NOISE. The row's other knobs are that oscillator's own:
DUTY
PULSE's: the pulse's width; 50% is the hollow square, the narrow ones thinner. (A table can move it: below.) 12.5%, 25%, 50%, 75%
WAVE
WAVE's: which of the 16 waves it plays, by name (ORGAN ...); the WAVE page shows them.
SHAPE, STEPS, GATE
BUZZ's: SHAPE the envelope's shape (SAW DN, SAW UP, TRI), STEPS how many steps it has (16 or 32), GATE ON cuts it with a square at the same note (the "sync buzzer").
NOISE
The noise row. Its first knob, NOISE, ON mixes noise into the tone:
MODE
K2: LONG, a hiss; SHORT, a metallic, pitched noise. LONG, SHORT
RATE
K3: how high the noise sounds. 0-F
KEY
K4: KEY ON, the rate follows the note played; KEY OFF, it stays as set. KEY OFF, KEY ON
CLOCK
The row of the chip's own manners. Its first knob, CLOCK, is the chip it is tuned on (BRK, 8BIT, PSG 1.77, PSG 1.00, PSG 1.79, 16BIT), so high notes go out of tune as they did on that chip; EXACT is always in tune.
CURVE
K2: how its 16 volume steps sound, as on each chip. BRK, 8BIT, PSG, 16BIT
FILTER
K3: the chip's own output filter, or NONE. BRK, 8BIT, PSG, NONE
FRAMES
K4: how often its tables and envelopes step: 60 or 50 times a second, as the old machines' screens did. 60 HZ, 50 HZ
SWEEP
The sweep's row: the pitch slides by itself from each note's start. Its first knob, SWEEP, sets the way: OFF, DOWN or UP.
SHIFT
K2: how big each step of the slide is. 0-7
PACE
K3: how often it steps; 0, never. 0-7
VOLUME
The page of the volume. Its first row is named VOLUME too:
VOL
K1: the volume, in the chip's 16 steps. 0-F
ENV
K2: NONE, the volume stays; DOWN or UP, it steps down or up by itself; PSG, the chip's own envelope (the next row). NONE, DOWN, UP, PSG
STEP
K3: how often DOWN or UP takes a step. 0-7
RELEASE
K4: how fast the sound fades once the key is let go; 0 stops it at once. 0-F
PSG ENV
The PSG's envelope, used with ENV at PSG:
SHAPE
K1: one of the chip's 16 shapes, drawn beside its number: down, up, repeated, triangles. 0-F
PERIOD, FINE
K2 and K3: the envelope's speed, a four-digit hex number: PERIOD sets its first two digits, FINE its last two. Bigger is slower.
TABLES
The page of the tables: built-in lists that change the sound a step a frame (FRAMES: 60 or 50 a second).
VOL, ARP, PITCH, DUTY, NOISE
A row for each table: VOL shapes the volume, ARP adds notes (chords, drum drops), PITCH bends the pitch, DUTY changes the pulse's width, NOISE the noise's rate. Each row has the same two knobs:
TABLE
K1: which table, by number and name, or -- for none.
SPEED
K2: how many frames each step of it lasts. X1-X4
VIBRATO
The vibrato's row: DELAY (K1, how many frames after the note it starts, 0-62), SPEED (K2, X1-X4) and DEPTH (below).
DEPTH
K3: how far the pitch swings. 0-62 cents
WAVE page
The row TABLE: the wave the WAVE oscillator plays (00 SAW ...), drawn large.

Sampler

A sampler cartridge holds samples (recorded sounds, uploaded from the computer: the FM-1 does not record audio) and up to 64 instruments that play them. One sample can serve several instruments: a drum loop cut into hits, say. To bring your own sounds and make instruments for them, see chapter 17.

SAMPLE
The first page. Its first row is named SAMPLE too:
SAMPLE
K1: which of the cartridge's samples it plays. ENV on it lists the samples (name, length, rate, waveform): the keys play the one highlighted, and ENV again picks it.
START, END
K2 and K3: the part of the sample that plays, a click moving 1/200 of the sample (SEL held: 10 clicks).
LOOP
The loop's row. Its first knob, LOOP, sets how the part from FROM to TO repeats while the key is held: OFF, it plays once; FWD, over and over; PING, forwards and backwards in turn.
FROM / LOOP START, TO / LOOP END
K2 and K3: where the loop starts and ends (the header says LOOP START and LOOP END), a click 1/200 of the sample.
RELEASE
K4: how long the sound fades once the key is let go; ENDLESS lets it ring. 4 MS ... 118 S, ENDLESS
PITCH
The pitch's row:
BASE NOTE
K1: the note at which the sample plays as it was recorded. Set it to the note the recording sounds, and the keys play it in tune.
TUNE
K2: finer tuning, in 1/128 of a semitone, up to almost a semitone either way.
VOLUME
K3: the volume a note gets when its cell has none. Songs converted from MOD, S3M or XM files bring their samples' default volumes here; for your own sounds, leave it at 64. 0-64
ENVELOPE
The second page, an envelope as a DX7 operator's.
RATES, LEVELS
Two rows: RATES, R1 to R4 on K1 to K4, and LEVELS, L1 to L4. The volume rises to L1, goes on to L2, then L3, where it stays while the key is held; let go, it moves to L4. Each R sets how fast it moves to its L, 99 the fastest. 0-99

In the samples list, SEL, DELETE removes a sample. When instruments use it, it warns first (DELETE SAMPLE?, 3 INSTRUMENTS USE IT AND ARE DELETED TOO), and they go with it; an unused one goes at once (SAMPLE 03 DELETED). Deleting an instrument never deletes its sample: SETTINGS' CLEAN UP removes samples nothing uses.

FUSION

A FUSION instrument is a sound made of a pattern. Each key plays its own row of the pattern, every note of that row at once: C-4 plays row 3C (its MIDI note number), and letting go stops them all. So one key can play a chord, a layered sound, or a different drum on every key (a kit).

FUSION
The one page: the pattern's map above.
PATTERN
Which pattern it plays. On it, K1 or ENV pick another (in ENV's list the keys try each before you pick); SEL opens it in the EDITOR to write it.
  • Writing it: SEL on PATTERN opens the EDITOR on the pattern, locked to it: with REC off the keys play this FUSION as you write it, its rows lighting green; with REC on they write. HOME comes back.
  • EDIT on an empty FUSION slot makes a new pattern (128 rows, 4 tracks) and first asks (A NEW PATTERN FOR THIS SLOT, FILL IT WITH 01:00 EL PIANO?): K1 or SELECT pick another sound (the keys hear it); OCT+ (FILL) writes that sound's note on every row, so the slot plays as that sound, ready for layers; OCT- (EMPTY) leaves it empty.
  • Rows the keys do not reach can keep ideas for later; SEL, MOVE puts one on a key.
  • A FUSION inside a FUSION is silent: no chains, no loops. Voices are shared: rows with many notes take voices from other sounds.

The menus

SEL on a slot:

MARK
Several slots: SELECT (ALGORITHM by 8) stretches the mark; then SEL for their menu. COPY, INIT and DELETE act on all of them. SEL held + SELECT marks too.
COPY, PASTE
Copy a sound (4 at most) and paste it over a slot (COPIED 3; nothing copied: NOTHING COPIED).
MOVE, SWAP
MOVE carries the sound to an empty slot (full cartridge: NO EMPTY SLOT: SWAP INSTEAD); SWAP trades places. SELECT carries, SEL puts down, HOME takes back. Songs using it are asked about (references).
DELETE
Empties the slot.
INIT
A plain starting sound in the slot.
RENAME
Type its name.
AUTO LEVEL
As loud as the others.
REVERT
The sound as last saved (REVERT SLOT 01:00 TO SAVED?).

SEL in the cartridge list (ENV):

NEW
A new cartridge: pick its type (DX7, JUNO-106, TB-303, CHIP, SAMPLER, FUSION). It goes at the end of your cartridges (CARTRIDGE 11 MADE); all numbers used: ALL CARTRIDGE NUMBERS USED.
CLONE
A copy (01 CLONED TO 11). A sampler cartridge's samples are copied too, written at once (CLONING ITS SAMPLES); without room for them, NO ROOM IN THE USER AREA.
MOVE
To another free number; a sampler cartridge with unsaved changes must be saved first (SAVE IT FIRST).
DELETE, RENAME
As for a slot.
AUTO LEVEL ALL
Sets every sound's LEVEL at once, after a question (AUTO LEVEL 32 SOUNDS?, EACH ONE'S LEVEL SET AGAIN): LEVELS SET.
BACK TO BUILT-IN
On a changed built-in cartridge (brown number): your changes dropped, the firmware's own back.
REVERT
The whole cartridge as last saved.

Keys on INSTRUMENTS

K1 K2 K3 K4Change the row's four values, one a knob.
ALGORITHMTurns the pages of settings.
SEQTurns the pages too, round.
KEYSPlay the sound as it changes.

KEYSIn the samples list, play the sample highlighted. In the pattern list, try each pattern as this FUSION would play it. On a FUSION sound, each key plays its own row of the pattern.
ENVAgain: uses the sample, or the pattern, highlighted.
K1On a FUSION's PATTERN: steps to another pattern.

HOMEIn that EDITOR: back to the FUSION's settings.
