OCT-... or EMPTY, the pattern left empty.
K1 SELECTIn that question: offer another sound (K1 another cartridge's, SELECT the next sound).

PLAYBACK

PLAYBACK follows what plays: the pattern playing now, scrolling with the music, in the EDITOR's grid. Nothing on it can be changed by accident, so it is the screen to perform from: jump between positions, change the song's speed and volume, play over it. Open it with HOME + OP4.

What it shows

  • The pattern playing now, scrolling with the play position. There is no cursor and no editing.
  • The header shows the song position and the last one (02/0B); the footer's right side the position and row playing (POS 02 ROW 1F).
  • While the EDITOR's pattern loop plays, the header says PAT 0C (or EDITOR for its own pattern) and the footer PAT 0C ROW 1F.
  • While LOOPS' loops play, each loop is a track; the header says LOOPS. EDIT then goes to LOOPS.
  • When nothing plays, it shows where playback paused, or the current song's start; with no song at all, NOTHING HAS PLAYED: PLAY STARTS THE SONG.

SEQ (or K2) shows 8, 4, 2 or 1 tracks at once, as in the EDITOR (4 TRACKS). ALGORITHM moves the highlighted track across; the view scrolls sideways to keep it in sight.

Playing the song live

  • PLAY pauses and resumes what played last.
  • SELECT steps through the song a row at a time: the first click pauses and plays the current row again; each click forward plays the next row, each click back the previous one. PLAY goes on from there.
  • K1 jumps to another position of the song (K1 POSITION 03/0B PATTERN 05). While playing, the jump comes as the current row ends, and it is a clean start: every note of the song is cut and the effects' tails emptied. Paused, PLAY resumes from that position.
  • K3 is the song's volume, from +6 dB down to -24 dB and OFF, a dB a click (K3 VOLUME -6 DB). It turns the song alone, not the keys, so you can play over a quieter song.
  • K4 is the song's speed, in BPM, from 3 to 600 (K4 TEMPO 124.0 BPM -3.2%: the BPM, and the change against the song's own tempo). Every tempo the song plays is scaled by it, its tempo commands too.
  • LFO puts back the one of K3 and K4 turned last: the volume to 0 dB, the speed to 100 %.
  • The keys play the current instrument over the song; ARP arpeggiates them.
  • HOME + white key mutes and unmutes tracks.
The speed and the volume are not saved. They stay for every song you play until something else plays (the EDITOR's pattern loop, LOOPS, DJ), and at power-off they go back to 100 % and 0 dB.

More from PLAYBACK

  • EDIT opens the EDITOR on the pattern playing, with the cursor on the playing row; HOME comes back here.
  • ENV opens the song list: PLAY there plays the highlighted song from its start, and PLAYBACK follows it; ENV again closes the list.
  • GLO opens the view's options (PLAYBACK VIEW): SCROLL by ROWS (the playing row stays in the middle) or by PAGES (the highlight moves, the pages flip; also SETTINGS' PLAYBACK SCROLL), and UNLOAD SONG, listed once something has played: everything stops, and the keys get their own effects and tempo back, as at power-on (chapter 6).

Keys on PLAYBACK

KeyDoes
PLAYPauses and resumes what played last.
SEQShows 8, 4, 2 or 1 tracks at once, round.
K2Also changes the number of tracks shown: clockwise more.
ALGORITHMMoves the highlighted track across.
SELECTPauses, then plays the song a row a click; PLAY goes on from there.
K1Jumps to another position of the song.
K3The song's volume (the keys stay as they are).
K4The song's speed, in BPM.
LFOPuts the volume or the speed, whichever you turned last, back to 0 dB or 100 %.
EDITOpens the EDITOR on the row playing; HOME comes back here.
HOMEBack from the EDITOR opened with EDIT.
ENVOpens the song list; PLAY there plays a song from its start.
GLOThe view's options: scroll by rows or pages; UNLOAD SONG.
KEYS OCT- OCT+ PRESETSPlay the current instrument over the song, as on every screen.
ARPSwitches the arpeggiator on and off.
ARP heldWith SELECT, ALGORITHM or K1: the arpeggiator's rhythm, order and latch.

DJ

DJ turns the FM-1 into a DJ stand: two songs on two decks, kept in time, mixed with a crossfader, with a filter, loops, cue points and stops on each deck. It is only for performing: nothing done on DJ changes a song. Open it with HOME + OP5.

The stand

  • The left deck is the main: its tempo is the set's tempo, and the right deck can follow it (SYNC).
  • Each deck shows its song, its BPM and the change from the song's own tempo, its position and bar, an overview of the song with the time left, its filter, and its loop or repeat.
  • The crossfader (ALGORITHM) blends the two: all the way left, only the main is heard (as at first).
  • The song list below: SELECT moves its highlight; L, R or LR mark the songs on the decks.
DJ stays apart until it plays. Opening DJ changes nothing of what plays: you can set up the decks in silence and leave. DJ's first start (a deck's PLAY key, say) stops what was playing and cuts its sound, so the decks start dry. PLAY on DJ while something else plays first pauses it (PAUSED: PLAY AGAIN FOR DJ); the next PLAY plays the decks. Once DJ plays, the decks play on outside DJ until a song, a pattern or the loops start.

Loading and playing

  1. Turn SELECT to a song in the list.
  2. Press OP4 to load it on the left deck, or OP5 on the right (LEFT: CITY LIGHTS). A song with no positions is refused (SONG 0A IS EMPTY).
  3. Press OP1 to play or pause the left deck, OP6 the right. Held, the deck goes back to its song's start, paused (LEFT: BACK TO THE START).
  4. PLAY plays or pauses both decks at once; held, both go back to their cue points (BACK TO THE CUES).
  • Loading onto a playing deck waits for its next bar line (LEFT: CITY LIGHTS AT THE BAR; the LOAD key blinks): the new song takes over at the bar, at the BPM the deck was playing, so the beat goes on. Hold the LOAD key instead to have it start at its own tempo (LEFT: CITY LIGHTS AT ITS TEMPO). Tap LOAD again before the bar line to cancel (LEFT: LOAD CANCELLED).
  • The same song can be on both decks, to fade from one part of it to another.
  • At a song's end it loops or stops, as the song says. Stopped, its PLAY has nothing more to play (THE END: CUE GOES BACK). Through the last 8 bars of a song that stops, the time left turns red and the deck's PLAY key blinks on the beat.
  • An empty deck refuses PLAY, CUE, SYNC, HOLD and FILTER: NO SONG ON THE DECK.

SWAP: SEQ exchanges the decks (DECKS SWAPPED; both empty: NO SONGS TO SWAP): songs, places, cue points, tempos, filters, loops and mutes. Nothing heard changes. The usual flow: the main plays; you load the next song on the right, start it in time and bring it in with the crossfader; SWAP; the right deck is free for the next one.

Tempo and SYNC

  • K1 is the left deck's tempo (the set's), K4 the right's: shown as the BPM it plays and the change (TEMPO L 124.0 BPM +3.2%), 3 to 600 BPM in steps of 0.1 (SEL held: 1 BPM). The song's own tempo commands still act, scaled. SEL after a turn sets it back to the song's own (TEMPO 120.0 BPM: THE SONG'S).
  • MONO is SYNC (on at first): the right deck follows the main's tempo (or its half or double, whichever is nearest its own song's) and its beats fall on the main's. A synced right deck starts on the main's next bar line; its tempo knob then does nothing (SYNC: TEMPO ON THE MAIN DECK). SYNC ON, SYNC OFF.
  • With SETTINGS' SYNC set to EXTERNAL, an outside MIDI clock leads the main deck (SYNC EXTERNAL: THE CLOCK'S TEMPO); START plays it from its cue point, STOP pauses it.
  • Two decks at one BPM never drift apart.

Filters, volumes and effects

  • K2 is the left deck's DJ FILTER, K3 the right's: one way a low-pass (LP, darker), the other a high-pass (HP, thinner), OFF in the middle (FILTER L LP 2.4K).
  • OP3 (the left) and the black key GLO (the right) switch the filter off and back on, sliding there while the key is held (FILTER L OFF, FILTER L ON LP 2.4K). With the filter off, the knob sets the filter silently, ready for the key to bring it in on the beat.
  • ENV switches K2 and K3 to the decks' VOLUME and back (K2 K3: VOLUME, K2 K3: FILTER): +6 dB down to -24 dB and OFF, a dB a click (VOLUME L -3 DB).
  • SEL tapped puts the last knob turned back: a tempo to the song's own, a filter to OFF, the crossfader to the middle, a volume to 0 dB, a KEY to 0.
  • Each deck plays its song's mixer and its own GATE, FILTER, DRIVE, LO-FI and DUCK. CHORUS, DELAY and REVERB are DJ's own, shared by both decks, with DJ's settings: FX on DJ edits them, with the LIMITER and the METRONOME, and FX again comes back to DJ.
  • FX + white key held plays a punch-in over the mix, as everywhere.
  • When all 16 voices are busy, the deck the crossfader favours less gives way.

A hand on the record: HOLD

OP2 is the left deck's HOLD, PIT the right's:

  • Held down, the deck stops where it is, as a hand on the record.
  • Turn the deck's tempo knob meanwhile (K1 left, K4 right): it moves by hand, a row a click, heard. Its filter knob (K2, K3) moves it silently, a beat a click, for the long way.
  • Let go: a deck that was playing plays on from there at once. So a tap holds a deck back by that much, to nudge it against the other.

The pads

The white keys are each deck's pads: keys 1-8 the left deck's, 9-16 the right's. The BLANK key turns their mode between PLAY pads and LOOP pads (PADS: PLAY, PADS: LOOPS); LFO brings in the LFO pads.

Pad (left, right)PLAY pads
1 9SET CUE: sets the cue point on the bar line nearest the tap, while the deck plays on (CUE: POS 02 BAR 4). Held a quarter second, on the beat instead.
2 10CUE: as a DJ player's CUE. Paused, sets the cue point. Playing, plays from the cue point while held, and pauses there when let go. Press the deck's PLAY key while CUE is held, and it plays on when you let go.
3 11JUMP: back to the cue point, playing on; held, the jump lands on the next beat.
4 12MOVE: held, the deck's knobs move a cursor: K1 (the left deck's; K4 the right's) a bar a click, and K2 (K3) a pattern a click (MOVE L POS 03 BAR 2); let go, the deck moves there on the next beat, in phase, playing on.
5 13BRAKE: held, the deck slows and its pitch falls, a turntable's stop.
6 14BACKSPIN: held, the record spun back by hand.
7 15ECHO OUT: held, the deck's sound goes into the delay and stops on the next beat, the echoes ringing on.
8 16REVERB OUT: the same into the reverb.

The stops (pads 5-8) work while held: let go, the deck plays on where it would have been, in time, as if it had never stopped; a tap is a dip. Press the deck's PLAY key while a stop is held and the deck stays stopped when you let go.

Pad (left, right)LOOP pads
1 9PATTERN: the deck's current pattern over and over, on or off (LEFT: REPEAT PATTERN ON).
2 3 4REPEAT 4, 2, 1 BARS (the left deck; 10-12 the right's): the block of bars the deck is in, round and round until tapped again.
5 6 7 8A free LOOP of 2 bars, 1 bar, 1/2 bar, 1/4 bar from the last beat (13-16 the right's).
white key heldA ROLL: any loop pad held is a loop for as long as it is held; let go, the deck plays on from where the loop is.

A loop stays through a pause; a pad that cannot act (a stop on a paused deck, say) blinks fast.

The LFO pads

LFO brings in the LFO pads (PADS: LFO), and LFO again goes back. They make things swing by themselves, each at a note length of the tempo (1/2 at first). Hold LFO to see which pad does what.

PadLFO pads
1The crossfader's LFO on / off (FADER LFO: TRIANGLE 1/2, FADER LFO OFF).
2Its shape: SINE, SQUARE, TRIANGLE, SAW UP, SAW DOWN, RANDOM.
3Its range: MIRROR (through the middle), L TO HERE, L TO R, SWING.
4Reverse: HERE TO R, R TO L.
5 6 7The left deck's filter LFO: on / off, shape, range (OFF TO HERE, OFF TO FULL, HERE TO FULL, SWING).
8Held: K1 turns the left deck's KEY a semitone a click, -6 to +6, its tempo kept (KEY L +1), to mix in key.
9 10 11The right deck's filter LFO, the same.
12Held: K4 turns the right deck's KEY.
13 14 15The FX LFO, swinging DJ's REVERB MIX (or DELAY, CHORUS: GLO's FX LFO): on / off, shape, range.
16Every LFO off (ALL LFOS OFF).
1 5 9 13 heldHold an LFO's on / off pad and turn ALGORITHM: its speed, from 32 BARS to 1/8 (FADER LFO 1/4). SEL after: back to 1/2.

Mutes, the CUT, saving

  • HOME + white key mutes a deck's track: keys 1-8 the left deck's tracks 00-07, keys 9-16 the right deck's (LEFT TRACK 02 MUTED). SEQ first, or the key held: solo (LEFT TRACK 02 SOLO).
  • HOME + OCT+ takes those keys to tracks 08-0F (MUTES: TRACKS 08-0F); HOME + OCT- back (MUTES: TRACKS 00-07). Alone, OCT does nothing on DJ.
  • HOME + PLAY takes both decks back to their cue points; HOME + REC cuts the sound while the decks play on.
  • SAVE keeps the whole stand (the decks as they stand, the crossfader, SYNC, the LFOs): at power-on the decks are back, paused, and PLAY goes on from the same point.

DJ's properties

GLO opens DJ PROPERTIES:

CROSSFADER
SMOOTH (each deck at -3 dB in the middle, as loud through the blend) or SHARP (both full until the last 2 clicks at either end, for cuts).
FILTER RESONANCE
The DJ filters' resonance. 0-100 %
FILTER THE SENDS
ON: a deck's filter also filters what it sends to the shared effects, so a sweep takes its echoes along. OFF saves some processor time. ON, OFF
FX LFO
What the FX LFO swings. REVERB MIX, DELAY MIX, CHORUS MIX
RESET DJ
EDIT, after a question (RESET DJ?, BOTH DECKS EMPTIED, ALL AS AT FIRST): both decks emptied, everything as at first (DJ RESET).

VISUAL

VISUAL shows the sound: each voice's wave, the output as an oscilloscope, a scrolling waveform, a spectrum, a meter for each track, and FOMA, PT/FM's mascot. Open it with HOME + PIT.

The views

SELECT turns the views a step at a time (it stops at both ends); SEQ goes to the next and round. The header names the view (VISUAL SCOPE).

VOICES
A small scope for each voice, labelled with what plays it (T03 a song's track, KEY the keys, L05 a loop) and its note.
SCOPE
The output as an oscilloscope, left above, right below.
WAVE
The output's waveform over the last seconds, scrolling.
SPECTRUM
The output's spectrum: bass on the left, treble on the right (30 Hz to 18 kHz).
LEVELS
A meter for each track, 00 to 0F.
FOMA
PT/FM's mascot: a little FM-1 with a cat's ears, flying into the stars, its rainbow tail waving with the sound.

Zoom, gain and options

  • K1 zooms SCOPE in time, 1 to 6 (K1 ZOOM 3): from 128 to 1,024 samples across the screen.
  • K2 makes every view taller or flatter, x0.13 to x16 in doublings (K2 GAIN X1).
  • GLO opens VISUAL OPTIONS: VIEW STEREO or MONO, and FREEZE OFF or ON, to hold the picture still (the footer then says FROZEN).

VISUAL works from a copy of the sound, never slowing it down.

Keys on VISUAL

KeyDoes
SELECTTurns the views, a step at a time.
SEQThe next view, round.
K1Zooms SCOPE in time.
K2Makes the view taller or flatter.
GLOThe options: stereo or mono view, freeze.
PLAYPauses and resumes what played last.
KEYS OCT- OCT+ PRESETSPlay the current instrument, as on every screen.
ARPSwitches the arpeggiator on and off.
ARP heldWith SELECT, ALGORITHM or K1: the arpeggiator's rhythm, order and latch.

STATUS

STATUS is the start screen: the FM-1 opens on it (unless SETTINGS' POWER-ON SCREEN says otherwise). It shows PT/FM's version and how to get help, and the figures behind the header: how busy the sound keeps the processor, the voices, the storage and memory, the device. Open it with HOME + GLO.

The pages

SELECT or ALGORITHM turns the pages:

PT/FM
The name, the version, PRESS HOME + LFO FOR HELP, and the figures a glance needs:
CPU 1, MAXHow much of its time the first processor spends on the sound now, and the most since the last reset. Green up to 50 %, yellow to 80 %, red above.
CPU 2The same for the second processor (effects and voices 11-16); OFF while it does not run.
HALFThe longest piece of sound work, in microseconds: over 5804 is too slow.
LATEPieces of sound not ready in time: each one is a click (dropout).
STEALSNotes that gave their voice up to a new note because all were busy.
VOICES, MAXVoices sounding now and the limit (01/12), and the most at once.
EDITS FREEThe memory left for unsaved edits.
FLASH FREEThe free storage, where saves go.
UNSAVEDHow many things changed since the last SAVE.
BATTERY, UPThe battery, and the time since power-on.
SONGThe song playing, else the current song.
PERFORMANCE
Each processor's load now, on average and at most; the worst sound piece, late pieces and steals; each engine's share; voices; the effects' cost; a graph of the last 30 seconds.
STORAGE
The user area (where everything you keep goes), used and free; what it holds by kind; unsaved changes and the memory they take.
USER FLASH MAP
The user area as a map, a square a kilobyte, each in the colour of what it holds.
RAM MAP
The FM-1's 512 KB of memory as a map, a square a kilobyte.
DEVICE
The battery, the firmware version, the output (stereo, mono, sync pulse), MASTER, the screen's frames a second, the time since power-on, VOICES, THEME and the second processor's state. SECOND CORE reads STARTING in the first two seconds, then ON; OFF when SETTINGS' SECOND CORE is off; or, in red, why it stopped until the next start: STOPPED: NO ANSWER, STOPPED: MISREAD, STOPPED: STUCK, STOPPED: FAULT, or STOPPED: AFTER A CRASH (after PT/FM crashed, the second processor stays off until the FM-1 is switched off and on). Without it, the FM-1 plays on with 12 voices at most. BATTERY reads 1, 2 or 3 bars, or USB POWER.

The footer's right side shows the free storage (FREE 237K).

SETTINGS

SETTINGS holds the FM-1's global settings and the tools that look after your storage. It has two pages: the list, and MIDI. Open it with HOME + MONO (or EDIT on STATUS).

Changing a setting

  1. SELECT picks a setting; the footer shows its default (DEFAULT STEREO).
  2. K1 changes it, a step a click. It applies at once.
  3. LFO puts it back to its default.
  4. SAVE keeps the settings after power-off, as every change.

SEQ or ALGORITHM turns to the MIDI page and back. SEL, REVERT takes the page back to what was saved, after a question (REVERT THE SETTINGS TO SAVED?); with nothing unsaved, NOTHING TO REVERT.

Sound and output

OUTPUT
What the jack and the speaker get. STEREO for headphones and a mixer. MONO for the FM-1's own speaker, which plays one channel only (and for a mono cable). SYNC PULSE L or R: a click on that side every half beat, for instruments that follow a sync pulse, the music in mono on the other side (with SYNC INTERNAL only; with SYNC EXTERNAL the output stays stereo, no clicks). A cable in the jack mutes the speaker, and the FM-1 cannot tell, so set this yourself. STEREO, MONO, SYNC PULSE L, SYNC PULSE R; STEREO at first
LINE GAIN
The level of the speaker and the jack, with MASTER. -24 to +12 dB, 0 dB at first
USB GAIN
The level of USB audio, the sound a computer records; MASTER does not touch it. -24 to +12 dB, 0 dB at first
VOICES
How many notes are heard at once, everywhere. 16 needs the second processor (SECOND CORE); while it does not run, 16 counts as 12 (16 VOICES: 12 WITHOUT CPU 2). When all are busy, a new note takes the voice least missed: a ringing tail first, then the quietest held note; the keys' notes go last. A held note pushed out comes back when a voice frees. 8, 12, 16; 16 at first
SECOND CORE
The FM-1's chip has two processors: ON works the effects and voices 11-16 out on the second. OFF: one does it all (12 voices at most). ON, OFF; ON at first
TUNING
The pitch of A4. 430-450 Hz, 440 at first

The keys, the knobs and the look

THEME
The screen's colours. DEFAULT, EGA, PASTEL, NEON, SUNSET, ICE, CLEAR, GREEN, AMBER, WHITE, DAYLIGHT, PAPER, MANUAL, SILVER, LCD, COMMANDER; DEFAULT at first
KEYS VOLUME
The volume of the notes the keys play and write (the keys have no velocity). 01-7F, 60 at first
KEYS GAIN
How loud you hear the keys while playing them (the FM-1's and MIDI's), not how they are recorded. -24 to +12 dB, 0 dB at first
KEYS
THROUGH FX: the keys go through the effects as everything else. DRY: past every effect, straight to the output. THROUGH FX, DRY; THROUGH FX at first
KEYS OCTAVE
The keys' octave at power-on. -4 to +4, 0 at first
KNOB SPEED
Bigger steps when a knob is turned fast. OFF, LOW, HIGH; LOW at first
HOLD DELAY
How long a button must be held to count as held. 300-1500 ms, 500 at first
COMBO GRACE
How long a button let go still counts for a combination. 0-250 ms, 100 at first
PLAYBACK SCROLL
PLAYBACK scrolls by ROWS (the playing row stays in the middle) or by PAGES. ROWS, PAGES; ROWS at first

Recording and the arpeggiator

COUNT-IN
Before an EDITOR take: 1 or 2 bars of clicks, none, or KEY (your first note starts the take). LOOPS has its own. OFF, 1 BAR, 2 BARS, KEY; 1 BAR at first
QUANTIZE
Where an EDITOR take puts a note: on the nearest line of 2, 3 or 4 rows, the nearest row, or REAL TIME (the row it falls in, its exact time kept with a note delay). The keys sound exactly as written. 2 ROWS, 3 ROWS, 4 ROWS, ROW, REAL TIME; ROW at first
ARP RHYTHM
The arpeggiator's rhythm and the EDITOR's row preview, a row a step: # plays, _ rests. #, #_, #__, #___, ##_, ###_, ##__, #_##_, and two slow ones; #___ at first
ARP PATTERN
The order the arpeggiator's notes take turns in. UP, DOWN, UP-DOWN, RANDOM, AS PLAYED; UP at first
ARP LATCH
How many notes go on playing after you let go of their keys. OFF, 1-8 NOTES; 4 NOTES at first
POWER-ON SCREEN
The screen the FM-1 starts on. STATUS, LAST, or any screen; STATUS at first

TOOLS and ABOUT

On TOOLS, K1 picks a tool and EDIT runs it:

TOOLS
The line of tools below.
CHECK REFERENCES
Lists the references to things that are missing (a note's instrument gone, a song's pattern deleted): MISSING REFERENCES: 3, or NO MISSING REFERENCES.
CHECK STORAGE
Reads every saved record and checks it is whole (CHECKING STORAGE): STORAGE OK, or a list of problems (STORAGE PROBLEMS: 2). It writes nothing.
CLEAN UP
Finds what nothing uses and asks what goes, as a checklist (CLEAN UP: FREES 1.3K): UNUSED PATTERNS, UNUSED SAMPLES (ticked at first), UNUSED INSTRUMENTS (not: most of a bank is a library, not leftovers). SELECT picks a line, K1 ticks it, OCT+ cleans up (CLEANED UP: 4 DELETED; nothing to do: NOTHING TO CLEAN UP). Built-in things are never listed.
AUTO LEVEL ALL
Measures every sound you have and sets its level, after a question; the built-in cartridges keep theirs.
REVERT ALL
Drops every unsaved change, after a question, as SAVE + OCT- does.
FACTORY RESET
Erases everything you saved or uploaded: songs, patterns, loops, your cartridges and samples, your edits of the built-in instruments, DJ's decks, the settings and the MIDI map. PT/FM itself and its built-in instruments stay, so the FM-1 is as it was after its first install, before the demo disk.

It asks twice. First FACTORY RESET? with ERASES ALL YOU SAVED OR UPLOADED and ONLY THE BUILT-IN INSTRUMENTS STAY: OCT+ answers RESET. Then ERASE IT ALL NOW? with THERE IS NO WAY BACK, and, if you have changes not saved yet, how many go with the rest (3 UNSAVED CHANGES LOST TOO): OCT+ answers ERASE. OCT- (KEEP) or HOME at either question leaves everything as it was.

Then ERASING shows a bar for up to two seconds, the sound silent and every control waiting, and the FM-1 restarts on its power-on screen with the settings as they come.

To keep a copy first, read the FM-1 on the editor page and download a disk (chapter 17). The demo songs come back with the install page's UPLOAD DEMO DISK (chapter 2). A power cut while it erases leaves part of your work: run FACTORY RESET again.

ABOUT
EDIT opens it: the version and the licences. EDIT closes it.

The MIDI page

The second page (SEQ), the same kind of list (chapter 16 explains MIDI in full):

MIDI IN CHANNEL
The channel MIDI in listens to, on USB and the jack. ALL, 1-16; ALL at first
MIDI OUT
What goes out over USB: OFF, KEYS (the FM-1's keys as played) or ALL (the keys and everything that plays: track 0 on channel 1 ... track 15 on channel 16). OFF, KEYS, ALL; KEYS at first
MIDI OUT CHANNEL
The keys' channel out. 1-16; 1 at first
SYNC
INTERNAL: PT/FM's own tempo. EXTERNAL: an outside MIDI clock leads (USB or the jack). INTERNAL, EXTERNAL; INTERNAL at first
CLOCK OUT
Sends the clock, START / STOP / CONTINUE and the song position out, with SYNC INTERNAL. OFF, ON; OFF at first
MIDI CONTROLLER
EDIT turns the FM-1 into a MIDI controller for a computer until it is switched off and on, after a question (chapter 16).
LEARN
How many mappings of 64 (3 OF 64). EDIT learns one: touch an FM-1 control, then move the MIDI control that should drive it (TOUCH AN FM-1 CONTROL, MOVE THE MIDI CONTROL). The mappings are listed below; LFO deletes the one picked.

Keys on SETTINGS

KeyDoes
SELECTPicks a setting (on MIDI, then the mappings).
K1Changes it, at once; on TOOLS, picks the tool.
LFOPuts it back to its default; on a mapping, deletes it.
SEQ or ALGORITHMTurns to the MIDI page and back.
EDITRuns the tool picked; opens and closes ABOUT; on MIDI CONTROLLER, switches; on LEARN, learns.
SELREVERT: the page's own back as saved (the settings; on MIDI, the mappings).
SAVEKeeps the settings after power-off.
ARPSwitches the arpeggiator on and off.
ARP heldWith SELECT, ALGORITHM or K1: the arpeggiator's rhythm, order and latch (also set here: ARP RHYTHM, ARP PATTERN, ARP LATCH).

LOOPS

LOOPS is a loop station: you record a layer in one pass, then the next over it, without stopping the music. You keep a stack of up to 16 loops, mute and solo them while playing over them, and can record the whole performance as a new song. Open it with HOME + POLY.

The loops

  • Up to 16 loops, listed in the order they were made, the newest at the bottom, with + NEW LOOP under them. A loop's number is its place, 00 to 0F.
  • One length for all, set by the first loop in whole bars (8 bars at most at 1/16). After that only the properties' LENGTH and the menu's DOUBLE change it.
  • A loop has one instrument and a colour of its own. PRESETS (and ENV, the cartridges) pick the sound the keys play and the next loop takes, never a recorded loop's.
  • POLY or MONO, chosen before recording (the black keys MONO and POLY in CONTROL mode; POLY at first): a POLY loop holds up to 4 notes at once, a MONO loop one, a note over a held one taking over as the properties' MONO LEGATO says.
  • A loop's mix: K1 to K4 turn the selected loop's LEVEL, PAN, DELAY SEND and REVERB SEND (CHORUS and DUCK on FX's MIXER). On + NEW LOOP they set the next loop's mix.
  • ALGORITHM turns the tempo, any time.
  • LOOPS has its own effects (FX from LOOPS edits them) and metronome, so it sounds the same whatever song is current. SAVE keeps the loops like any change.
What plays (a song, a pattern) plays on into LOOPS until the loops start. The loops play on outside LOOPS until a song or a pattern starts. Leaving LOOPS for any screen but FX ends a take.

Recording a loop

  1. Pick a sound with PRESETS. Turn SELECT to + NEW LOOP (for a new loop) or to a loop (to record it again).
  2. Press REC: the take is armed.
    • With the loops playing, it starts at their next start; the row counts down (ARMED: STARTS IN 3 BARS).
    • With nothing playing, your first note starts the loops and the take at once; or press PLAY to start them after the properties' COUNT-IN.
  3. Play. A take is one pass of the length and stops by itself, the loops playing on. Press REC to stop it early; REC while armed cancels (CANCELLED).

The first loop has no length to fill: it grows a bar at a time while you play. Press REC to close it on a bar line (LOOP 00: 4 BARS); its bars are the length. Played nothing: NOTHING PLAYED: NO LOOP. PLAY with no loops, nothing armed and nothing playing is refused: REC, THEN PLAY: THE FIRST LOOP.

  • What you hear is what is kept. While recording, notes land on QUANTIZE's grid and sound there; a MONO loop plays one note at a time, a POLY one at most 4. Not recording, the keys play freely.
  • RE-RECORD: EDIT (or REC on a loop) records the selected loop again; its old notes are gone the moment the take is armed (LOOP 03 RE-RECORDING). It keeps its place, colour, instrument and mix.
  • PEEL: LFO removes the selected loop (on + NEW LOOP, the last) without asking (LOOP 03 PEELED); SEL's REVERT brings back what was saved.
  • A full edit memory ends a take, keeping what was written (MEMORY FOR EDITS IS FULL).

QUANTIZE

Where a recorded note lands: the properties' QUANTIZE, or the black keys OP1-OP5 in CONTROL mode (QUANTIZE: 2 ROWS).

2 ROWS, 3 ROWS, 4 ROWS
The nearest line of that many rows, from the loops' start.
ROW
The nearest row (at first).
REAL TIME
The row it falls in, its exact time kept as a note delay, its end as a key off.

A note played a little early waits for its line; one just after it sounds at once and is written on the line.

CONTROL mode: mutes and solos

In CONTROL mode the keys stop playing notes and become a mixer for the loops. Each white key is a loop: white key 1 is the top loop, white key 16 the sixteenth.

  1. Press SEQ. The FM-1 shows KEYS: CONTROL and the header reads SEQ MUTE.
  2. Tap a white key: its loop mutes (LOOP 02 MUTED) or plays again (LOOP 02 ON) at once.
  3. Press SEQ again to play notes: KEYS: PLAY.

Hold a white key a moment instead (longer than HOLD DELAY in SETTINGS) and the change waits for the next bar line (LOOP 02 MUTED AT THE BAR); the loop's row shows a yellow M while it waits.

Press the black key GLO to make the white keys solo instead of mute (SEQ: SOLO; again: SEQ: MUTE). One loop is soloed at a time: a white key solos its loop alone (LOOP 02 SOLO), and on the soloed loop it ends the solo (LOOP 02 SOLO OFF). Held, the solo waits for the bar line (a yellow S).

While a loop is soloed only it sounds, but the mutes are kept and come back when the solo ends. SAVE keeps the mutes with the loops; a solo is never saved, so after a power-on no loop is soloed.
KeyIn CONTROL mode
white keyIts loop: mute or unmute (in SOLO: solo, or end the solo) at once.
white key heldThe same at the next bar line; held again, the wait is called off.
OP1 OP2 OP3QUANTIZE 2, 3 or 4 rows.
OP4 OP5QUANTIZE a row; REAL TIME.
PITEvery loop back on: all mutes and the solo cleared (ALL LOOPS ON).
GLOThe white keys mute, or solo.
MONO POLYHow the next loops record: one note at a time, or up to 4 (NEXT LOOPS: MONO, NEXT LOOPS: POLY; the footer shows it).
SEQBack to playing notes.

From any screen, HOME + white key mutes or unmutes that loop at once; hold the white key to solo it.

The pattern recorder

ARP opens a step sequencer over the loops, which play on, so the pattern is heard in the mix while you build it. (The EDITOR's SEL, RECORD PATTERN is the same recorder.)

  • 4 rows of 16 steps, a note a row (with a kit, each row a drum). SELECT picks the row; a white key switches its step on or off.
  • The row's note: K3 moves it a semitone a click; or tap SEL, then press a key: that key is the note (KEYS: THE NOTE, then KEYS: THE STEPS). SEL held + a key does it at once. OCT- / OCT+ move the row's note with the octave (NOTE C-5).
  • K1 STEP SIZE (1/32 to 1/4, 1/16 at first), K2 LENGTH (4, 8, 12 or 16 steps), K4 TIMES (x1-x8, for the first loop only: how many times it fills the new length).
  • GLO: the notes RING TO THE NEXT (at first) or last A STEP LONG (NOTES RING TO THE NEXT, NOTES A STEP LONG).
  • The preview plays while the recorder is open; ARP switches it off and on.
  • REC writes it and closes: on + NEW LOOP a new loop (PATTERN: LOOP 06, 4 BARS); opened on a loop, it replaces that loop's notes (PATTERN INTO LOOP 03). No step on: NO STEPS ON. HOME closes it, nothing written.

What you set stays for the next time until power-off.

RECORD LIVE: the performance as a song

SEL, RECORD LIVE records everything you do over the loops into a new song: the loops as they play, mutes and solos, the keys, effects, punch-ins, tempo changes and the mix.

  1. SEL, RECORD LIVE opens its panel: the song's NAME (EDIT types it) and K1 TEMPO.
  2. REC arms it (REC blinks; the top line's REC reads SONG). HOME cancels.
  3. It starts with your next REC, a note, or PLAY.
  4. Perform. PLAY drops the loops out and brings them back; PLAY held takes them to their start; the keys play on their own tracks.
  5. REC ends it (SONG 12 RECORDED: 1:23, 5 PATTERNS). SAVE keeps the song.
  • While a song records, nothing changes the loops themselves: takes, PEEL, DOUBLE and the like are refused (RECORDING A SONG).
  • Leaving LOOPS (but for FX) ends it, keeping what was written.
  • Notes that do not fit the song's 16 tracks are left out and counted (SONG 12: 3 NOTES LEFT OUT). It stops by itself when the memory, the pattern numbers or 256 positions run out (SONG 12 STOPPED: MEMORY FOR EDITS IS FULL); with no song number free it is refused (NO SONG NUMBER FREE).

Loops to a pattern and back

LOOPS has no precise editing; for that, store the loops in a pattern and edit it in the EDITOR.

SAVE TO PATTERN
Writes one pattern of the loops' length: every loop's notes, repeats written out, each with its instrument, and each loop's mix (LOOPS STORED IN PATTERN 2A). Pick NEW or a pattern; a pattern that is not empty asks first.
LOAD FROM PATTERN
Turns a pattern into loops, a loop an instrument, replacing the loops after a question (PATTERN 2A IN LOOPS: 3 LOOPS). The length is the pattern's, in whole bars; what does not fit 16 loops of 4 notes is left out and said.

The properties and the menu

GLO opens LOOPS PROPERTIES:

TEMPO
As a song's, with its BPM (ALGORITHM turns it too). 3-600
SWING
50-75 %
LENGTH
A bar more or less: longer adds silence at the end, shorter cuts bars off (asking first when notes would go). Before the first loop: THE FIRST LOOP SETS IT.
GRID
1/16, 1/16T or 1/32: 4, 6 or 8 rows a beat. Only before the first loop (GRID: ONLY BEFORE THE FIRST LOOP).
QUANTIZE
Where a recorded note lands (above): on every 2, 3 or 4 rows, on the nearest row, or where you played it (REAL TIME). 2 ROWS, 3 ROWS, 4 ROWS, ROW, REAL TIME; ROW at first
MONO LEGATO
On a MONO loop, a note over a held one: GLIDE (a short glide; a TB-303's slide), LEGATO (the held note moves to the new one, no new attack) or JUMP (a plain new note).
COUNT-IN
Before a take PLAY starts: OFF, 1 BAR, 2 BARS. A key always starts at once. OFF at first

SEL opens the menu:

APPLY INSTRUMENT
The selected loop takes the current instrument (LOOP 03: 01:04 BRASS).
DOUBLE
The length x2, every loop playing twice what it played (DOUBLED: 8 BARS; past 8 bars: DOUBLE: AT MOST 8 BARS).
RECORD LIVE
Its panel (above); while armed, CANCEL RECORD LIVE.
SAVE TO PATTERN, LOAD FROM PATTERN
Above.
CLEAR LOOPS
Every loop goes, after a question; the next loop sets a new length (LOOPS CLEARED).
REVERT
LOOPS as last saved, after a question.

With no loops, EDIT, LFO and the menu's loop items say NO LOOPS YET.

FX

FX holds the effects on the whole mix, the mixer, the metronome and the punch-in effects. Press FX on any screen to open it, and FX again to go back where you were. SEQ turns its three pages: LIVE, EDIT and MIXER.

Whose effects

Every song has its own effects (its FX setup: the chain's order, routing, each effect's knobs and on/off, the mixer and the metronome). LOOPS and DJ have their own. FX always edits what you hear:

  • the song playing (or the one played last); a pattern from the EDITOR uses the current song's;
  • in LOOPS, the loops'; on DJ, DJ's (FX from LOOPS or DJ does not leave them);
  • before anything has played, THE KEYS': the keys' own setup, with the reverb on, so the FM-1 sounds round as a synth from its keys alone.

A new song starts with only the LIMITER on. THE KEYS' setup, which the keys play through at power-on, also has the REVERB on. While what FX edits plays, nothing but your hand changes the effect under the cursor: the song's own commands for it are skipped.

The keys keep the last song's effects. Once a song has played, the keys go on playing through its effects and at its tempo after it stops or pauses, until something else plays. THE KEYS' own setup comes back at the next power-on, or at once with UNLOAD SONG (SONGS' SEL menu, chapter 6). With LOOPS on the screen and nothing playing, the keys play through the loops' setup.

LIVE: playing the effects

  • The white keys are the 16 punch-in effects, each while its key is held (below); the keys play no notes on LIVE.
  • The black keys pick an effect, a fixed key each: OP1 GATE, OP2 FILTER, OP3 DRIVE, OP4 LO-FI, OP5 CHORUS, OP6 DELAY, PIT REVERB, GLO LIMITER, MONO DUCK, POLY METRONOME.
  • The BLANK key is BYPASS: every effect off while held (the metronome clicks on).
  • SELECT picks the effect too. OCT+ switches it on, OCT- off (GATE ON, GATE OFF).
  • K1 to K4 turn its knobs (SEL held: steps of 10); ALGORITHM shows its next knobs (FILTER has 8, DELAY 5). LFO resets the knob turned last.
  • EDIT shows the effect on the EDIT page; SEL opens its menu (RESET, REVERT).
  • ARP on LIVE plays the last note you played, hands free (with SETTINGS' ARP LATCH not OFF), so you can play the effects over an arpeggio: the keys stay punch-ins.

EDIT: the chain

  • The chain is a list: the sound goes from top to bottom. The LIMITER is always last; DUCK and the METRONOME sit apart, outside the chain.
  • SELECT picks an effect; K1-K4 its knobs; ALGORITHM its next knobs.
  • OCT+ / OCT- switch it on and off, so you can set it first and switch it on after. The keys play notes on EDIT, to hear the effect; SEL + OCT+ and SEL + OCT- change their octave.
  • SEL opens the menu: MOVE (SELECT moves the effect through the chain, heard as it goes; SEL puts it down, MOVED; HOME puts it back, NOT MOVED; the LIMITER, DUCK and the metronome stay: LIMITER DOES NOT MOVE), RESET (the effect as at first), REVERT (every effect as last saved).
  • Each effect's picture shows what it does: the filter's curve, the echoes, the reverb's decay. The footer shows what the effect costs the processor (GATE 0.4% CPU). Each effect, its picture and its knobs are below.

The effects

Ten effects, each in a section of its own below, in the order FX EDIT lists them, with all its knobs. On EDIT, SELECT picks the effect, K1-K4 turn its first four knobs and ALGORITHM shows the next four (FILTER and DELAY have more than four); LFO puts the last knob turned back to its default. A knob with no range given runs 0-100 %. A new song starts with only the LIMITER on (THE KEYS' setup has the REVERB on too); OCT+ switches the picked effect on.

GATE

Chops the sound on and off in a rhythm, locked to the song's bars: a trance gate on whatever passes through it. Its rhythm is a pattern of 16 steps; each step is OFF (closed), ON (open for the first three quarters of the step) or a ratchet, X2, X3 or X4 (two, three or four short hits within the step).

PATTERN
Which rhythm. 00-0F are built in (the table below); 10-1F are yours, MY GATE 10 to MY GATE 1F, written on the white keys (below). 00-1F; 00 STRAIGHT at first
RATE
How long a step is: at 1/16 the 16 steps make one bar of 4 beats, at 1/8 two bars, at 1/32 half a bar; 1/8T and 1/16T are triplet steps (3 and 6 to a beat). At 1/16, step 1 falls on the bar's first beat. 1/8, 1/16, 1/32, 1/8T, 1/16T; 1/16 at first
DEPTH
How far a closed step closes: 100 % is silence, 50 % only dips the sound, 0 % leaves it as it is. 100 % at first
SMOOTH
How soft the edges are: low, a hard click-on, click-off chop (0.5 ms); high, a soft pulse that swells in and out (up to 20 ms). 20 % at first
No.PatternIts 16 steps (# open, . closed, 2 / 3 ratchets)
00STRAIGHT################: every step, a steady chop
01OFFBEAT.#.#.#.#.#.#.#.#: only the steps between
02TRANCE#.###.###.###.##: the classic trance gate
03HALF##..##..##..##..: two open, two closed
04GALLOP#.##.##.#.##.##.: a galloping rhythm
05SKIP##.##.##.##.##.#: threes skipping across the beats
06SPARSE#...#...#...#...: one hit a beat
07ROLL####2222####3333: a roll building up
08STUTTER2.2.2.2.2.2.2.2.: double hits, every other step
09DOTTED#..#..#..#..#..#: every third step, dotted eighths
0ASYNCOPE#..#.#..#..#.#..: syncopated
0BPULSE###.###.###.###.: three open, one closed
0CRAMP#.#.##.####.####: denser across the bar
0DBREAK########........: the bar's first half, then silence
0ETRIPS3.3.3.3.3.3.3.3.: triple hits, every other step
0FCHOP##..#.#.##..#.#.: a chopped break

Writing your own steps: on EDIT with GATE picked, EDIT puts its 16 steps on the white keys: a key switches its step on or off; held, ALGORITHM gives it ratchets (X2, X3, X4). A built-in pattern is copied into yours first (STRAIGHT COPIED TO MY GATE 11). EDIT keeps the changes, HOME drops them. ENV on GATE lists the patterns.

FILTER

One filter on the whole mix: a low-pass (darker, the top taken away) or a high-pass (thinner, the bass taken away), with an envelope that can open it on every note or beat, as a synth's filter envelope does. Its eight knobs are on two pages (ALGORITHM turns to the second).

CUT
Where the filter cuts, and which kind: turned left of the middle it is a low-pass closing from LP 20K down to LP 100 (Hz); turned right, a high-pass opening from HP 20 up to HP 8.0K; in the middle, OFF. Turned by hand it glides, so no step is heard. With the envelope on, CUT is where the filter rests between notes. LP 100 ... LP 20K, OFF, HP 20 ... HP 8.0K; OFF at first
RESO
Resonance: a peak at the cutoff. Low is smooth; high makes the cutoff ring and whistle, the acid squelch when the cutoff moves. 30 % at first
ENV
How far each note (or beat) opens the filter, as a part of the way from CUT to fully open: a low-pass opens upward, a high-pass downward. 0 % switches the envelope off. 0 % at first
SOURCE
What opens it. KEYS: every note the keys play (the FM-1's, MIDI's, the arpeggiator's), held as long as the key. TRACK 00 ... TRACK 0F: every note that track starts, muted or not, so a silent track can carry a rhythm for the filter. 4 BEATS, 2 BEATS, BEAT, 1/2 BEAT, 1/4 BEAT: the beat itself, every so many beats, each hit held half its length. KEYS at first
ATTACK
How long the filter takes to open from where it is. 2 ms-3 s; 2.0 MS at first
DECAY
How long it then takes to close down to SUSTAIN. 5 ms-5 s; 296 MS at first
SUSTAIN
How open it stays while the note is held, as a part of ENV's opening; 0 % closes it fully after DECAY, a pluck. 0 % at first
RELEASE
How long it takes to close back to CUT once the note ends. 5 ms-5 s; 296 MS at first

There is one envelope for the whole mix, not one a note: each new note starts it again from wherever it is, and it holds while any note of the source is held.

LO-FI

The sound of an old sampler: fewer bits, a lower sample rate and record crackle.

BITS
How finely the level is measured: 16 is clean, 8 grainy, 4 and under harsh and noisy, 2 a broken buzz. 2-16; 8 at first
RATE
The sample rate it imitates: lower takes the top away and adds the metallic ring of aliasing; 44 kHz leaves the rate as it is. 1-44 kHz; 22 at first
DUST
Crackles and specks, as from a record. They are a sound of their own: heard even when nothing plays. 20 % at first

CHORUS

A JUNO-style chorus: two short delays, swaying in opposite ways left and right, mixed with the sound, so it widens, thickens and gently detunes.

MODE
The JUNO-106's three chorus settings. I: slow (0.5 Hz) and gentle. II: a little faster (0.83 Hz) and deeper, a lusher swirl. I+II: fast (9 Hz) and shallow, a shimmering vibrato. I, II, I+II; I at first
RATE
The sway's speed, around the mode's own: 50 % is the JUNO's, 0 % about a third of it, 100 % about 1.7 times. 30 % at first
DEPTH
How far it sways, around the mode's own in the same way: more is a stronger pitch wobble. 50 % at first
MIX
How much of the chorus is heard against the sound itself. With ROUTING SENDS (below) it is the chorus's return level instead, and each track sends to it by its MIXER send. 50 % at first

DELAY

Echoes locked to the song's tempo. The echoes are mono; PING-PONG puts them left and right in turn.

TIME
The time between echoes, as a note value; T marks triplets, a dot dotted values (1/8. is three sixteenths). Up to 1 s (0.5 s with PING-PONG): a value longer than that at a slow tempo plays the longest that fits. 1/32, 1/16T, 1/16, 1/8T, 1/16., 1/8, 1/4T, 1/8., 1/4, 1/2T, 1/4., 1/2; 1/8. at first
FEEDBACK
How much of each echo comes back as the next: low, one or two echoes; high, a long trail. 40 % at first
TONE
How bright each echo is: every repeat passes through a low-pass, so lower makes the echoes darker and softer as they go, as a tape or analogue delay; 100 % keeps them bright (up to about 13 kHz). 60 % at first
PING-PONG
ON: the echoes bounce between left and right. OFF: they stay in the middle. OFF, ON; OFF at first
MIX
How loud the echoes are against the sound. With ROUTING SENDS, the delay's return level instead. 30 % at first

REVERB

A plate reverb: the sound in a large, smooth, bright space.

SIZE
How long the reverb rings: from about 1.3 s, a room, to about 11 s, a cathedral (the time it takes to die away). 60 % at first
DAMP
How dark the tail gets: more damping takes the highs out of the tail as it rings, warmer and less hissy; none leaves it bright. 40 % at first
PRE-DELAY
A gap before the reverb starts, so the sound's attack stays clear in front of it. 0-100 ms; 10 at first
MIX
How loud the reverb is against the sound. With ROUTING SENDS, the reverb's return level instead. 25 % at first

DRIVE

Warm distortion: the mix pushed into a soft clipper, adding harmonics as an overdriven amplifier or tape does. The deep bass (under about 55 Hz) is kept out of it, so it stays clean; the level is evened out as the drive rises.

DRIVE
How hard it is pushed: low, a little warmth and grit; high (up to about nine times the level), heavy saturation. 30 % at first
TONE
The brightness after the distortion: low is dark and smooth, high bright and edgy. 50 % at first

LIMITER

Keeps the mix from going over a ceiling, catching its peaks so the sound never clips. Always last in the chain, and on in every new song.

CEILING
The most the mix may reach. Lower catches more of the peaks, and the mix comes out quieter. -12 to 0 dB; -1 at first
RELEASE
How fast the level comes back after a peak: short keeps it loud but can pump; long is smoother. 10-1000 ms; 100 at first

DUCK

One track pushes the others down while it plays, as a kick making room for itself in the bass and the pads (sidechain). It sits outside the chain. Which tracks duck, and how much, is set in the MIXER's DCK row, none at first: raise DCK on the tracks that should duck (MIXER). The source never ducks itself.

SOURCE
The track that pushes the others down, or KEYS: every note the keys play, so the song can make room for a part played live. 00-0F, KEYS; 00 at first
DEPTH
How far the others go down when the source hits (each also by its own DCK). 60 % at first
RELEASE
How long they take to come back up after it: short, a quick dip; long, a slow breathing pump. 20-1000 ms; 150 at first

METRONOME

A click on the beats, to play or record in time. It is mixed after the effects, takes no voice, and stays off USB audio. It sits outside the chain. The count-in before a take is not the METRONOME's: SETTINGS' COUNT-IN (chapter 13).

TEMPO
FOLLOW: the tempo of what plays (on THE KEYS, their own TEMPO). A number: its own tempo, so it clicks with nothing playing. FOLLOW, 30-300 BPM; FOLLOW at first
BEATS A BAR
How many beats a bar; the first is accented, louder and higher. In LOOPS it is also the loops' bar. 1-16; 4 at first
SOUND
CLICK: a short tick of noise. BEEP: a clean tone (higher on the accent). WOOD: a woodblock knock, its pitch falling. COWBELL: the classic drum machine's two-tone cowbell. CLICK, BEEP, WOOD, COWBELL; BEEP at first
LEVEL
How loud it clicks. 60 % at first

Routing and the keys

GLO opens FX PROPERTIES, titled whose setup it is (a song's name, THE LOOPS, DJ or THE KEYS):

ROUTING
GLOBAL: one chain on the whole mix. SENDS: CHORUS, DELAY and REVERB leave the chain and become shared sends, each track sending its own amount (the MIXER's CHO, DLY, REV); their returns join the chain at the SENDS line (marked with a diamond): effects above it work on the dry sound only, below it on everything (ROUTING SENDS, ROUTING GLOBAL).
KEYS, EVERYWHERE
THROUGH FX, or DRY: the keys skip every effect (as SETTINGS' KEYS) (KEYS DRY, KEYS THROUGH FX).
TEMPO, SWING
For THE KEYS: their own tempo and swing.

MIXER

  • A column for each of the 16 tracks (8 at a time), a row for each value: LVL (level), PAN, DCK (how much it ducks, shown while DUCK is on), and with ROUTING SENDS CHO, DLY, REV (its sends).
  • ALGORITHM picks the track, SELECT the value, K1 changes it (SEL held: by 16), LFO resets it.
  • KEYS, the last column, is the keys' own strip, the same in every song (its LVL is SETTINGS' KEYS GAIN).
  • In LOOPS the columns are the loops (MIXER: THE LOOPS).
  • A value a song's command moved shows white, BY THE SONG; muted tracks are dark.

Punch-in effects

Hold FX and press a white key, on any screen: that effect plays on the whole mix for as long as the key is held, locked to the tempo. On LIVE the white keys alone do it. Let go, it fades back into the mix.

KeyPunch-in
1 2 3 4Loops: LOOP 1/4, LOOP 1/8, LOOP 1/16, LOOP 1/32.
5 6 7 8Chops: STUTTER 1/16T, BIT CRUSH, GATE 1/16, GATE 1/32.
9 10 11 12Filters and space: LOW-PASS SWEEP, HIGH-PASS SWEEP, ECHO THROW, REVERB SWELL.
13 14 15 16Tape moves: REVERSE, HALF SPEED, TAPE STOP, VINYL STOP.
FX + white key heldA punch-in on any screen.
ARP, with a punch-in's key heldHolds the punch-in on after you let go of its key (LOOP 1/4 HELD ON: ITS KEY STOPS IT), so your hands are free; FX lights full meanwhile. Its key again (or another punch-in's) stops it, as does HOME + REC.

The song goes on underneath every punch-in, in time: let go, and you hear it where it is now, faded back in over 80 ms (VINYL STOP spins back up instead). FX LIVE's map shows short names (LP SWEEP, ECHO THRW, HALF SPD ...); FX held's list and the toasts, the full ones below.

LOOP 1/4, LOOP 1/8, LOOP 1/16, LOOP 1/32
Catch the last quarter, eighth, sixteenth or thirty-second note of the mix, just before the key, and repeat it for as long as the key is held: LOOP 1/4 repeats the last beat, as a DJ's loop does; LOOP 1/32 repeats so fast it becomes a buzzing roll.
STUTTER 1/16T
The same with a sixteenth-note triplet (a sixth of a beat): the fast, off-grid stutter of a glitch edit.
BIT CRUSH
The live mix ground down to a handful of levels (8 each way from silence, about 4 bits) at a sixth of the sample rate: gritty, aliased, old-sampler noise.
GATE 1/16, GATE 1/32
The live mix chopped on and off in time: sound for the first half of every sixteenth (or thirty-second) note, silence for the second, with soft edges. A trance gate on the whole song.
LOW-PASS SWEEP
A resonant low-pass filter closes over one bar, from 18 kHz down to 200 Hz, and stays closed while held: the song sinks under water.
HIGH-PASS SWEEP
A resonant high-pass filter rises over one bar, from 30 Hz up to 6 kHz: the bass and the kick fall away and the song thins to its top, the classic build-up before a drop.
ECHO THROW
Throws the mix into the delay while held: dotted-eighth echoes bouncing left and right, with 65 % feedback. Let go, nothing more goes in, and the echoes ring on for about 2.4 s over the song. It borrows the DELAY's line, so the song's own DELAY is not heard meanwhile.
REVERB SWELL
The mix rises into a huge reverb over two beats, the dry sound falling to half under it: a wash. Let go, its tail rings on in the song's own REVERB (with REVERB off, it fades out over 80 ms). It borrows the REVERB, so the song's own is not heard meanwhile.
REVERSE
The last beat played backwards, again and again while held.
HALF SPEED
The mix from the moment pressed, played at half speed: an octave down, dragging behind the song. It falls further behind the longer it is held, and every second it jumps back to the present, so each second held plays the half second that began it.
TAPE STOP
The sound slows down and stops over one beat, pitch falling with it, as a tape machine switched off. Stopped, it is silent until you let go.
VINYL STOP
A turntable's stop button: the record brakes to a standstill in half a second. Stopped, it is silent. Let go, it spins back up in a tenth of a second, straight into the song, landing on the beat.
TAPE STOP or VINYL STOP? Both slow the sound to a stop and stay silent while held. TAPE STOP follows the song: it takes one beat (half a second at 120 BPM, a whole second at 60), so it is slower than VINYL STOP in slow songs and faster in fast ones, and it simply fades back into the song when let go. VINYL STOP always takes half a second, whatever the tempo, and when let go it spins back up audibly, a DJ starting the record again.
The loops, the stutter, reverse, half speed and both stops play back the last half second of the mix, which the FM-1 keeps for them. In songs slower than about 120 BPM a whole beat does not fit in it, so LOOP 1/4 repeats an eighth note instead and REVERSE plays the last eighth backwards. The others (bit crush, the gates, the sweeps, the echo throw and the reverb swell) work on the live mix.

A pattern can hold punch-ins as commands (!08: as if its key were held for 8 rows), so songs can carry them. In LOOPS a punch-in is heard, and written only by RECORD LIVE.

Keys on FX

KeyDoes
FXOpens FX; again, back to where you were.
SEQThe next page: LIVE, EDIT, MIXER.
SELECTPicks an effect (on MIXER, the value).
K1 K2 K3 K4The effect's knobs (on MIXER, K1 changes the value).
ALGORITHMThe effect's next knobs (on MIXER, the track).
OCT+ OCT-Switch the effect on or off.
SEL held + OCT+ SEL held + OCT-On EDIT: the keys' octave.
LFOPuts the knob turned last back to its default.
SELThe menu: MOVE, RESET, REVERT.
EDITOn LIVE: the effect on EDIT. On EDIT with GATE picked: its steps on the white keys; again, keep them.
white key held, ALGORITHMOn GATE's steps: the held key's step gets ratchets, X2, X3, X4.
HOMEDrops GATE's step changes; during MOVE, puts the chain back.
ENVOn GATE: the gate patterns.
GLOFX PROPERTIES: routing, the keys, THE KEYS' tempo and swing.
white keysOn LIVE: the punch-ins. On EDIT and MIXER: play notes.
black keyOn LIVE: picks an effect.
BLANKOn LIVE: BYPASS while held.
KEYSOn LIVE no notes, only effects; on EDIT and MIXER they play.
ARPThe arpeggiator; with a punch-in's key held, holds the punch-in on.
ARP heldWith SELECT, ALGORITHM or K1: the arpeggiator's rhythm, order and latch.
HOME + white keyMutes a track (also on MIXER).

MIDI and USB

Connected by USB, the FM-1 is a sound card and a MIDI device for a computer or a phone, with nothing to install. The TRS MIDI IN jack takes a keyboard. SETTINGS' MIDI page (chapter 13) sets it all.

Playing PT/FM from MIDI

MIDI comes in over USB and through the MIDI IN jack (a TRS-to-DIN adapter, type A or B, for a keyboard's DIN cable); both behave the same.

  • Notes play as the FM-1's keys do, on every screen: they play the current instrument, write in the EDITOR with REC on, record into LOOPS, feed the arpeggiator. Velocity sets the note's volume. Every note plays, not only the keys' range.
  • MIDI IN CHANNEL picks the channel listened to (ALL at first).
  • Program change picks the instrument in the current cartridge, as PRESETS does: program n is the cartridge's n-th sound, counted from 0 and skipping empty slots, so it is not always slot n. Bank select (CC 0) picks the cartridge, as SEL + PRESETS does: bank n is the n-th cartridge in the cartridge list, counted from 0, not cartridge number n. With the demo disk, bank 0 is 01 DRUM KIT and bank 6 is F0.
  • Pitch bend bends the keys' notes, plus or minus 2 semitones. The sustain pedal (CC 64) holds the notes played from MIDI.
  • Every other controller does nothing until you learn it onto an FM-1 control (below).

MIDI learn

An outside controller's knobs and pads can work the FM-1's own controls: its 7 knobs, MASTER, every button but HOME (HOME cancels learning, so it cannot be learned) and the 27 keys. A learned control works exactly as the FM-1's, on every screen, with its combinations and holds.

  1. SETTINGS, the MIDI page (SEQ), turn SELECT to LEARN and press EDIT.
  2. TOUCH AN FM-1 CONTROL: turn the knob or press the button or key to learn (it does nothing else then).
  3. MOVE THE MIDI CONTROL: turn the outside knob, or press and let go the pad. The FM-1 works out what kind it is (an absolute knob, an endless encoder, a momentary or a toggle pad) and says what it learned (K1: CC 74, CH 1).

HOME cancels at either step. Up to 64 mappings; the list below LEARN shows them, and LFO deletes the one picked. SAVE keeps them.

MIDI out and the clock

  • MIDI OUT goes over USB only (the FM-1 has no MIDI OUT jack): OFF, KEYS (the FM-1's keys as played, on MIDI OUT CHANNEL) or ALL (also everything that plays: track 0 on channel 1 ... track 15 on channel 16). Notes that came in over MIDI are never sent back.
  • SYNC EXTERNAL follows an outside MIDI clock, from USB or the jack: its tempo, START, STOP, CONTINUE and the song position (a sequencer can start PT/FM from any bar). PT/FM locks to the clock itself, not only its tempo, so nothing drifts. In LOOPS the clock drives the loops; on DJ, the main deck. Lost for half a second, PT/FM plays on at the last tempo (CLOCK LOST).
  • CLOCK OUT ON sends the clock, START / STOP / CONTINUE and the song position, timed to the sound as heard.
  • SYNC PULSE: for instruments that follow a sync pulse through an audio cable, set SETTINGS' OUTPUT to SYNC PULSE L or R and use a stereo-split cable: a click on that side every half beat, the music in mono on the other. MASTER sets the clicks' level too. It works with SYNC INTERNAL only: while PT/FM follows a clock (SYNC EXTERNAL), the output stays stereo and sends no clicks.

USB audio

  • The FM-1 is a class-compliant USB audio input: no driver on Windows, macOS, Linux or a phone. Record it like any microphone or interface.
  • 16-bit stereo at 44.1 or 48 kHz, whichever the computer picks, kept in step with the computer's clock, so a recording never drifts or clicks.
  • It carries the mix after the effects, always stereo, at SETTINGS' USB GAIN (MASTER does not touch it). The metronome and the count-in's clicks stay off it.
  • No audio goes back from the computer to the FM-1.

MIDI CONTROLLER

The FM-1 can become a USB-MIDI controller for a computer: its keys, knobs and buttons send MIDI to a synth or a music program, and its screen shows what it sends.

  1. SETTINGS, the MIDI page, SELECT to MIDI CONTROLLER, EDIT. It asks first (SWITCH TO MIDI CONTROLLER?, PT/FM STOPS UNTIL THE FM-1 IS SWITCHED OFF AND ON), then whether to save unsaved changes (SAVE BEFORE SWITCHING?).
  2. PT/FM stops. The screen asks for the mode: REC for MIRROR (channel 16), HOME for GENERAL (channel 1); SELECT first picks another channel.
  3. Play. Switch the FM-1 off and on to get PT/FM back.
GENERAL
A keyboard controller: the keys send notes (OCT- and OCT+ shift them, -3 to +3, both together back to 0); K1-K4 send CC 74, 71, 73, 72 (cutoff, resonance, attack, release); SELECT CC 1 (modulation); ALGORITHM CC 21; PRESETS program change; MASTER CC 7 (volume); PLAY starts and stops a music program (MIDI Machine Control, and CC 114); the other buttons CC 102 and up.
MIRROR
Every control sends one fixed message, for working the virtual FM-1 of PT/FM's web pages from the real panel; the page lights the FM-1's LEDs back.

Nothing is saved in controller mode, and nothing is written to the FM-1's memory.

The EDITOR page

The EDITOR page, editor.html, is PT/FM's page for the computer (Chrome or Edge, offline). It comes with PT/FM, as install.html does: get it from PT/FM's home, hitosu.github.io/ptfm. It backs up the FM-1, brings new content to it (tracker modules, MIDI files, DX7 cartridges, sounds), and edits it with the FM-1's own pictures. It is a beta: its two panels are finished, its edit tabs work with plain controls.

Two panels

  • TABLE (left): everything you drop on the page, kept in the browser. Its items have no numbers, so it holds any number of songs, patterns and cartridges, and two imported modules never clash.
  • FM-1 (right): an image of what an FM-1 holds, with its numbers.
  • Drag items between the panels (or use the arrows): an item moves with everything it uses (a song with its patterns, their instruments, their samples), and numbers are given as it lands on the FM-1 panel. DELETE removes items; UNDO takes back any step.
  • Both panels group their items by kind: SONGS, PATTERNS, CARTRIDGES, SAMPLERS, SAMPLES and SYSTEM (the settings, the MIDI map, the loops, DJ's setup, the EDITOR's own pattern and the keys' song). A click on a group's header folds or opens it. Each panel shows its items as DETAILS (a row each, with sizes and what uses them), LIST or ICONS.
  • Picking works as in a file manager: a click picks one item, Ctrl adds one, Shift a range, Ctrl+A all. A double-click (or Enter) opens the item's tab, Space plays it, Delete deletes it, F2 renames it; the right-click menu has the rest.
  • The space bar under the FM-1 panel shows the FM-1's room: 103 blocks of 4 KB, as data, audio and free. Keep at least 16 blocks free for the FM-1's own saves: with fewer than 10 free, the FM-1 cannot save new things (it can still delete), and with fewer than 3 it cannot save at all until a WRITE frees room.

An item's tab

Every item opens in a tab of its own: double-click it, or EDIT IN A TAB in its menu. The tab edits a copy: SAVE puts the changes into the item, on its panel, and closes the tab; closing a tab with changes not saved asks SAVE, DISCARD or KEEP EDITING. A change saved on the FM-1 panel reaches the FM-1 only with WRITE. The pictures in a tab are the FM-1's own, drawn by PT/FM's own code exactly as the FM-1's screen shows them, and they follow the controls as you move them.

Song
Its properties (NAME, TEMPO, TICKS A ROW, ROWS A BEAT, SWING, AT THE END), its order (each position's pattern from a list, moved, removed or added), TRIM (tick the positions to keep), the MIXER (each track's LEVEL, PAN, DUCK and SENDS) and the FX setup (the chain's order by dragging, each effect on or off, its knobs).
Pattern
The grid, made for the mouse and the finger: a click picks a cell, a drag marks a block. The cell's panel has a keyboard of the FM-1's 27 keys with NOTE OFF and NO NOTE, the instrument picked from a list of the cartridges by name, the volume, and up to four commands, each with its meaning in words. On the computer's keyboard, the arrows, Page Up / Page Down, Home, End and Tab move; the letter keys write notes as the FM-1's keys play them (Z S X D C F V ... from F-3); = writes a note off; Delete clears; Ctrl+C, Ctrl+X and Ctrl+V copy, cut and paste; Space plays.
Instrument
Its NAME, LEVEL (AUTO LEVEL measures it as the FM-1 does) and its engine's parameters, each page beside the FM-1's picture of it. Every instrument page has a keyboard of the FM-1's 27 keys, played by mouse, touch, the computer's keys, or a MIDI keyboard picked from the computer's inputs. With VIRTUAL MIDI KEYBOARD picked, the computer's keys play anywhere in the tab (Z S X D C ... from F-3 as the FM-1's keys; [ and ] change the octave).
Sample
Its waveform with START and END to drag (or drag across it for a new cut), PLAY THE CUT, CHANNELS (both mixed, left or right of a stereo sound), RATE, DEPTH (8 or 16 bits), TRIM SILENCE, WHOLE SAMPLE, the sizes before and after, and the instruments that play it. Their START, END and loop points follow a cut when you SAVE. OPTIMIZE (below) makes it smaller.
SETTINGS, MIDI MAP, LOOPS, DJ SETUP
Every setting (and your 16 GATE patterns as rows of steps), each MIDI mapping, each loop's instrument and notes, and DJ's crossfader, filter, decks and effects.

Your own sounds

A sound dropped on the page becomes a sample, a recording. To play it from the FM-1's keys it also needs an instrument that plays it: the instrument sets its note, loop and envelope. The page does not make one for you. On the page:

  1. Drop the sound (WAV, FLAC, MP3, OGG ...) on the TABLE.
  2. Drag it onto a sampler cartridge of the FM-1 panel: it joins that cartridge. (Dragged onto the panel anywhere else, it gets a new sampler cartridge of its own.)
  3. Open the sampler cartridge's tab: beside the sample, NEW INSTRUMENT FOR IT makes the instrument. Set its BASE NOTE (the note the recording plays at its own pitch) and its loop, then SAVE.
  4. WRITE.

Or make the instrument on the FM-1, after the WRITE: INSTRUMENTS, the sampler cartridge, an empty slot; SEL, INIT makes a plain instrument there; EDIT, and on its SAMPLE row ENV lists the cartridge's samples (the keys play the one highlighted, ENV picks it). Set its BASE NOTE and loop, then SAVE (chapter 8).

Making room

Samples take most of the FM-1's room. The page can make them smaller: in a sample's tab, OPTIMIZE offers three levels, each with its size and what it saves, heard before you SAVE:

LOSSLESS
Changes nothing you hear: it cuts what no instrument plays (before the first START, after the last END or LOOP END) and the silent tail.
SMALLER
Adds the rate the page proposes for the sound (the lowest that loses nothing heard).
SMALLEST
Adds 8 bits, a softer top, and a level 6 dB lower, made up by the instruments' LEVEL.

On the TABLE, OPTIMIZE SAMPLES does the same to every sample picked (and every sample of a picked sampler) at once, listing each level's size before and after. UNDO takes it back.

Reading, writing and backing up

Connect the FM-1 by USB with PT/FM running. Nothing stays connected: each action finds the FM-1, does its work and lets go.

READ
Reads what the FM-1 holds into the FM-1 panel (after the first time, only what changed).
WRITE
Makes the FM-1 hold exactly the panel. Before writing it shows what it writes and what it removes (in red), warns when the FM-1 saved something since the last READ (READ FIRST, WRITE ANYWAY or CANCEL) and when fewer than the 16 advised blocks would stay free, and offers to back up first: what the write would replace goes onto the TABLE (BACKUP and the time). The FM-1's sound stops while it writes. With unsaved edits on the FM-1 it is refused: SAVE OR REVERT FIRST.
REVERT
Puts back what the panel showed after the last READ or WRITE.
DOWNLOAD DISK
Saves the FM-1 panel as a disk file (ptfm-2026-10-26.ptfmdsk). This is the backup: READ, then DOWNLOAD DISK.
UPLOAD DISK
Puts a disk file in the FM-1 panel, numbers kept; WRITE then puts it on the FM-1. A backup put back is exactly as it was.
Before installing another FM-1 firmware, READ and DOWNLOAD DISK: other firmwares erase PT/FM's memory.

Bringing content in

Drop files on the TABLE (or + ADD FILES):

Disks
.ptfmdsk files: their items as they are.
Tracker modules
MOD, S3M and XM: the song, its patterns (a channel a track, 16 at most), a sampler cartridge with every instrument and sample. IT is not read; XM's envelopes are not kept.
MIDI files
A song: each channel's notes become tracks, notes on the nearest row, the tempo kept, patterns of 4 bars; each channel's instrument mapped onto a built-in sound (all 128 General MIDI programs have one), the drums onto FM DRUM KIT. Pitch bend and controllers are left out.
DX7 cartridges
.syx, the 32-voice dump: a DX7 cartridge, exactly; a single voice's dump: a cartridge of one.
Sounds
WAV, FLAC, MP3, OGG and the rest: a sample, at the lowest rate that loses nothing heard.

Take only a part (some patterns, a cut of a sound) in the item's tab, then move it to the FM-1 panel and WRITE.

Every shortcut

Every key, combination and hold, screen by screen: the key tables of the chapters, gathered in one place. On the web page, point at a row and its keys light on the FM-1.

On every screen

KeyDoes
KEYSThe keys play the current instrument, unless the screen gives them another job (on LOOPS' CONTROL mode, DJ and FX's LIVE page, for example).
PRESETSPicks the current instrument: the sound the keys play. It goes round within its cartridge.
SEL + PRESETSPicks another cartridge (a bank of sounds): the cartridge list opens, and each click shows the next one. Hold SEL, or tap it first.
OCT- OCT+Shift the keys an octave down or up, from -4 to +4.
SEL + OCT- SEL + OCT+On FX's EDIT page, where OCT alone switches the effect off and on, these change the octave instead.
PLAYPlays, or pauses, what the screen plays (or what played last).
PLAY heldStops: what plays goes back to its start.
PLAY REC KEYSThese act the moment you press them, for timing. Every other button acts when you let it go.
SAVESaves all your changes. Its light is dim while something is not saved. While music plays, the save waits for a pause.
SAVE + OCT+Saves too: use it when you held SAVE so long that letting go no longer counts as a tap.
SAVE held + OCT-REVERT ALL: throws away every change since the last save, after asking.
FXOpens the FX screen; press it again to go back.

Every message

The messages the FM-1 shows, in the header for two seconds (toasts) or in a question, grouped by where they come up, with what each means and what to do. Numbers and names in them change with the case.

On every screen

MessageMeans
OCT +3The keys' octave changed (OCT- / OCT+).
TRACK 02 MUTEDHOME + a white key muted that track.
TRACK 02 ON... and unmuted it.
TRACK 02 SOLOThe track is soloed (HOME + white key held, or SEQ first).
SOLO OFFThe solo ended: every track plays again.
BACK TO THE STARTHOME + PLAY, or PLAY held: back to the start.
NO SONG TO PLAYPLAY with no song (or a song with no positions): make one on SONGS, or upload the demo disk.
SOUND CUT: LET GO OF RECHOME + REC: all sound is off while REC is held.
SOUND CUT, EFFECTS OFFREC held 2 s: every effect of what plays switched off (SAVE keeps it, REVERT undoes it).
ALL SOUND OFFEvery note and effect tail stopped at once.
CHANGES DROPPEDHOME left an edit, throwing its changes away.
SELECT MOVES IT, SEL PUTS IT DOWNA MOVE started: carry the thing with SELECT, put it down with SEL, HOME takes it back.
NOT MOVEDHOME during a MOVE: it is back where it was.
SELECT, ALG: MARK SEL: ITS MENUMARK started: stretch the mark with SELECT and ALGORITHM, then SEL for its menu.
OCT+ OCT-Over a question's answers: the key that gives that answer (OCT+ yes, OCT- no).
ARP UP C-4The arpeggiator on, with its pattern (and, on FX LIVE, the note it plays hands free).
ARP OFFThe arpeggiator off.
LATCH 4 NOTESARP held + K1: how many notes go on after you let go.
LATCHED NOTES LET GOARP held + LFO: the latched notes stopped.
SECOND CORE STOPPEDThe second processor stopped and one core does it all (VOICES 16 counts as 12). It comes back at the next power-on; STATUS' DEVICE says why.
NOT NOW: THE FLASH IS BUSYThe FM-1 is writing its memory: try again in a moment.
TOO BIG FOR ONE RECORDThe thing would be too big to keep in one piece: make it smaller (fewer tracks or rows).

Saving and reverting

MessageMeans
SAVING 3 CHANGESA save is being written.
SAVEDEverything is saved.
NOTHING TO SAVESAVE with nothing changed.
SAVE WAITS FOR A PAUSESAVE while playing: it is written when the music pauses (SAVE blinks meanwhile). Pause, or it is lost at power-off.
SAVE FAILEDThe save could not be written: try again; if it keeps failing, run SETTINGS' CHECK STORAGE.
SAVE: THE STORE IS BUSYSomething else is being written: SAVE again in a moment.
A SAVE IS UNDER WAYA save is still running: wait for it.
MEMORY FOR EDITS IS FULL SAVE BEFORE MAKING MORE EDITS 23 UNSAVED CHANGESThe memory for unsaved edits is full: OCT+ (SAVE NOW) saves, then make the edit again; OCT- goes back.
SAVE CHANGES TO FREE MEMORYThe memory for unsaved edits is three quarters full: a SAVE empties it. Shown at most once a minute.
NOT ENOUGH STORAGE TO SAVE 12 KB MORE NEEDED CLEAN UP FREES 30 KBThe save does not fit: OCT+ runs CLEAN UP; or delete something and save again. Nothing is lost meanwhile.
REVERT TO SAVED? DROP 3 UNSAVED CHANGES AND RELOAD FROM FLASHREVERT ALL asks: OCT+ drops every change since the last save.
REVERTED TO SAVEDREVERT ALL done.
NOTHING TO REVERTNothing has changed since the last save.
FACTORY RESET? ERASES ALL YOU SAVED OR UPLOADED ONLY THE BUILT-IN INSTRUMENTS STAYSETTINGS' FACTORY RESET asks first: OCT+ (RESET) goes on to the second question, OCT- keeps everything.
ERASE IT ALL NOW? THERE IS NO WAY BACK 3 UNSAVED CHANGES LOST TOOFACTORY RESET's last question (the third line only with changes not saved): OCT+ (ERASE) erases everything you saved or uploaded and restarts the FM-1.
ERASINGFACTORY RESET is erasing: up to two seconds, then the FM-1 restarts.
REVERT PATTERN 0A TO SAVED?A screen's REVERT asks (also for a slot, a cartridge, a song, the loops, the settings): OCT+ REVERT, OCT- KEEP.
REVERT THE EFFECTS TO SAVED? FOR CITY LIGHTSFX's REVERT asks, naming whose effects.
REVERTEDThe thing is back as saved.
PATTERN 1A IS USED 3 TIMES UPDATE REFERENCES?You move or delete something in use: YES makes what uses it follow (and saves everything), NO leaves the old numbers, HOME cancels.
UPDATING 3 REFERENCESThe references are being updated and saved.
REFERENCES UPDATED, SAVEDDone: everything that used it follows, all saved.
CARTRIDGE F0 BUILT-IN AGAINBACK TO BUILT-IN: your changes to a built-in cartridge are gone.

SONG 00 DELETED, 4 PATTERNS TOO SONG 00 DELETED, 1 PATTERN TOOThe song is deleted with the patterns only it used.

K1: TRANSPOSE, SEL: DONETRANSPOSE: turn K1, SEL ends it.

NO INSTRUMENT HEREThe pipette found no instrument on the cell or its track.
SELECT, ALG: CELLS SELECT, ALG: FIELDSThe note editor: the knobs move to other cells, or back to the fields.

THIS: NOT IN THIS FIRMWARE YET EDITOR: NOT IN THIS FIRMWARE YET FX: NOT IN THIS FIRMWARE YETThat part is not in this version of PT/FM.

LOOPS

MessageMeans
LOOP 00: 4 BARSThe first loop closed: its length.
NOTHING PLAYED: NO LOOPThe first loop closed with no notes: play something next time.

LOOP 03 MUTED LOOP 03 ONA loop muted or back on.
LOOP 03 MUTED AT THE BAR LOOP 03 ON AT THE BAR... at the next bar line (the key was held).
LOOP 03 SOLO LOOP 03 SOLO OFF A loop soloed, or its solo ended.
LOOP 03 SOLO AT THE BAR LOOP 03 SOLO OFF AT THE BAR... at the next bar line.
ALL LOOPS ONEvery mute and the solo cleared.

NO LOOPS YETThe action needs a loop: record one first.

DOUBLE: AT MOST 8 BARSThe length cannot double further (128 rows at most).

NOTES RING TO THE NEXT NOTES A STEP LONGThe pattern recorder's note length.

PATTERN INTO LOOP 03... or replaced a loop's notes.
RECORDING A SONGRECORD LIVE runs: the loops cannot change until it ends (REC).
SONG 12 RECORDED: 1:23, 5 PATTERNSRECORD LIVE wrote the song (SAVE keeps it).
