When something is wrong

What to look at first when the FM-1 does not do what you expect, from the sound to the flash. Each answer points to the chapter that tells the whole story.

The sound

What happensWhat to do
No sound at all.Turn MASTER up. A cable in the output jack mutes the speaker: unplug it to hear the speaker. SETTINGS' LINE GAIN sets the level of both (chapter 13).
On the speaker, some parts are missing.The speaker plays one channel only, so a part panned to the other side is not heard. Set SETTINGS' OUTPUT to MONO while you use the speaker, back to STEREO for headphones (chapter 13).
A track is silent.It may be muted, or another track soloed: HOME + white key switches a track's mute. While HOME's combination is open the white keys show the tracks: dim while a track plays, dark while it is muted, bright while it is soloed (chapter 4).
A note or a whole part plays nothing, and its instrument or pattern is drawn in red.It refers to something that is gone (an instrument, a pattern, a sample deleted or moved). SETTINGS, TOOLS, CHECK REFERENCES lists every such place (chapter 4).
The keys are too quiet or too loud against a song.SETTINGS' KEYS GAIN sets how loud the keys sound; KEYS VOLUME sets the volume of the notes they write (chapter 13).
Crackles or clicks in a busy part.Too much is asked of the FM-1 at once: many notes on heavy instruments with several effects on. Set SETTINGS' VOICES to 12 or 8, keep SECOND CORE on, or switch off an effect you do not need (chapter 13). STATUS shows how busy each processor is (chapter 12).
A computer records the FM-1 too quietly or too loud.SETTINGS' USB GAIN sets USB audio's level; MASTER does not touch it (chapter 16).

Starting and installing

What happensWhat to do
The screen says PT/FM CRASH.PT/FM stopped on an error. The FM-1 restarts by itself after a few seconds; what was saved is kept, edits not saved are lost. Until you switch the FM-1 off and on, it runs on one processor (VOICES 16 plays 12 voices at most; STATUS' DEVICE says STOPPED: AFTER A CRASH). If it happens again, note the numbers on the red screen.
The FM-1 does not start, or starts in USB RESCUE.After two failed starts in a row the FM-1 waits in USB RESCUE for an install. Install the firmware again from the install page (chapter 2). To reach USB RESCUE yourself, hold OCT- while switching on.
An install was cut short (a cable pulled, the power lost).It does not go on by itself. Press INSTALL FIRMWARE again, from USB RESCUE if need be (chapter 2).
The install page finds no FM-1.Close whatever else uses its MIDI port (a music program, another installer, another browser tab) and try again; use a USB cable that carries data (chapter 2).
An upload is refused with SAVE OR REVERT FIRST.The FM-1 has edits not saved: press SAVE (or revert them), then upload again (chapter 2).
The FM-1 shows DATA NOT RECEIVED: TRY AGAIN after an upload.The upload stopped half way. What was there before is whole, unless a nearly full FM-1's library was being replaced; either way, upload again.

Saving and storage

What happensWhat to do
Work is gone after switching off.Only what SAVE wrote survives power-off. The SAVE light is dim while something is not saved (chapter 4).
MEMORY FOR EDITS IS FULLThe working memory for changes is full. Answer SAVE NOW (OCT+), then make the edit again. STATUS' EDITS FREE shows the room left (chapter 12).
NOT ENOUGH STORAGE TO SAVEThe flash is full. Answer CLEAN UP (OCT+) to delete what nothing uses, or delete songs, patterns or samples yourself, then save again; nothing is lost meanwhile. STATUS' FLASH FREE shows the room left (chapter 13).
SAVE FAILEDSave again. If it keeps failing, run SETTINGS, TOOLS, CHECK STORAGE, which lists anything damaged (chapter 13).
You want to start from nothing.SETTINGS, TOOLS, FACTORY RESET erases everything you saved or uploaded; the built-in instruments stay. Download a disk first on the editor page to keep a copy (chapter 13, chapter 17).

MIDI and sync

What happensWhat to do
A keyboard plays nothing.Check SETTINGS' MIDI IN CHANNEL: ALL hears every channel, a number only that one. A keyboard's DIN cable goes into the MIDI IN jack through a TRS-to-DIN adapter, of type A or B (chapter 16).
An outside knob does nothing.Only notes, program change, bank select, pitch bend and the sustain pedal work by themselves; learn any other control onto an FM-1 control first (chapter 16).
PT/FM does not follow a sequencer's clock.Set SETTINGS' SYNC to EXTERNAL, and let the sequencer send its clock to the FM-1, over USB or the jack (chapter 16).
CLOCK LOSTThe outside clock stopped for half a second; PT/FM plays on at the last tempo. Start the clock again (chapter 16).
A computer gets no notes from the FM-1.Set SETTINGS' MIDI OUT to KEYS or ALL; MIDI out goes over USB only (chapter 16).

The instruments and the demo disk

What PT/FM brings: the built-in instruments, always there, and the demo disk, which the install page uploads (chapter 2). Cartridges and songs are listed by the numbers they show on the FM-1.

The built-in instruments

Eleven synth cartridges are part of PT/FM itself, numbered F0 to FA. They are there after every install, after CLEAN INSTALL and after FACTORY RESET. Your edits of them are saved apart, and BACK TO BUILT-IN drops them (chapter 4).

No.CartridgeEngineInstrumentsWhat
F0KEYS/ORGANSDX732Pianos, electric pianos, clavinets and harpsichords, organs, an accordion.
F1BELLS/PLUCKSDX732Marimbas, vibraphones, glockenspiels, celestas, bells and chimes, plucks.
F2GUITAR/STRGSDX732Guitars, harps, kotos, a sitar, a banjo; strings, solo and in sections.
F3WINDS/BRASSDX732Brass, flutes and pipes, reeds and saxophones, bagpipes.
F4PADS/CHOIRSDX724Choirs and voices, pads, an orchestra hit.
F5LEADS/BASSESDX732Saw, square, sync and sine leads; FM, synth and acoustic basses.
F6FM DRUM KITDX732Kicks, snares, claps, hats, cymbals, toms and hand drums.
F7PERC/FXDX732Percussion (triangles, whistles, agogo, surdos) and effects.
F8JUNO-106JUNO-106128Keys, organs, mallets, plucks, strings, choirs, brass, pads, stabs, leads, basses, drums, effects.
F9CHIPTUNECHIP128The sound chips of the 8-bit era in four families (BRK, 8BIT, PSG, 16BIT): leads, echoes and keys, arpeggios and chords, basses, pads and bells, kicks and snares, hats and percussion, effects.
FATB-303TB-30364Acid: saws, squares, squelches, basses, plucks, sweeps.

Drums, chip sounds, pads and effects all come from these engines. The demo disk's samples are only what the engines cannot make: natural instruments and real voices.

The demo disk's cartridges

No.CartridgeEngineInstrumentsWhat
01DRUM KITsampler10An acoustic kit: kick, snare, hats, crash, shaker, three toms.
02PERCUSSIONsampler11Wind chimes, darbuka, three congas, bongo, tabla, timpani.
03BAND/ORCHsampler15Piano, vibraphone, guitars, violins, tenor sax, flute, upright bass, and muted or short strokes of them.
04VOICESsampler6Dance shouts, a warning, a count-in.
05BASSsampler4Dubstep basses (a wobble, a "yoi" and a growl), a drum and bass bass.
06FUSIONFUSION6Layered instruments, below.

The FUSION cartridge's six instruments are layers of the others (chapter 8); their patterns are E0 to E5.

SPACE PAD
Two pads and a deep bass on every key, a bell from C-4 up.
DUB CHORDS
A minor 9 chord, rolled, with a sub bass, on every key.
SPLIT
A held bass under C-4, a space lead from C-4 up.
CHIPIN
A chip arpeggio on any key in C minor pentatonic, its echo, a triangle bass on C, a blip.
COIN
A game's coin on any key: a square a fourth under the key for a moment, then the key's note ringing out.
DRUM KIT
A drum on every key from F-2 to G-8, made of the synth cartridges' drums and the DRUM KIT and PERCUSSION samplers. The kick is on C-4, with the General MIDI drum kit's order from B-3 to G-5 and hand percussion on the six keys under it; fills, rolls, a flam and a drag on the octave under; the DRUM KIT sampler's drums alone on the octave over (C the kick, D the snare, F# and A# the hats, the toms between); the TB-303's drums above that, then hand drums and chimes. Each drum rings out however short the tap.

The demo songs

Six songs, each showing one part of PT/FM in one style: six patterns of 8 bars played once (about a minute and a quarter to two minutes), then they stop.

No.SongShowsStyle
00PUNCH INThe effectsDub techno into progressive house, F minor, 124 BPM: DUCK, FILTER, GATE, the punch-ins, a VINYL STOP ending.
01SPICE ROADThe samplersA band in D Dorian turning to D Hijaz: tablas, flute, a tenor sax solo.
02MIDNIGHT RUNThe JUNO-106Outrun synthwave, F# minor, 130 BPM: a galloping bass, the filter, chorus and pulse width turned by commands, a lead solo.
03CITY LIGHTSThe DX7 cartridges80s synthpop, D minor, 120 BPM: a sequenced FM bass, a staccato hook, brass stabs, orchestra hits.
04ACID TESTThe TB-303Acid techno into acid trance, A minor, 138 BPM: accents, slides, the knobs turned by commands, the DRIVE.
05ADVENTURECHIPTUNEGame music through time, 132 to 160 BPM: one theme through the eras of the sound chips, a time machine between them, coins, home again.

The DJ loops

Twelve loops for DJ's decks (chapter 10): each an 8-bar pattern that loops (DNB, ROCK, METAL and CHIP LOOP two: a verse and a bridge). All are in A minor, so any two mix in key (WORLD LOOP's flute aside: its B flat and C sharp go with the others' drums and bass, not their hooks), and at the same loudness. Each track plays one instrument, so LOOPS can load a pattern of them as loops, a loop a track (chapter 14), and every loop keeps the same tracks: 1 the kick, 2 the hats, 3 the bass, 4 the hook, then the rest. TECHNO, ACID, DISCO, DNB, ROCK and METAL LOOP start with an intro of 8 bars, played once, to mix in over the other deck.

No.SongShowsStyle
06TRANCE LOOPThe JUNO-106Psytrance, 140 BPM: a rolling bass after each kick, a squelching pluck.
07BREAKS LOOPThe samplersBreakbeat, 124 BPM: the DRUM KIT's break, a walking upright bass, a vibraphone riff.
08TECHNO LOOPThe DX7Techno, 126 BPM: the FM DRUM KIT, an FM bass after the kick, a pluck brightening and darkening.
09ACID LOOPThe TB-303Acid house, 128 BPM: a 303 line with accents and slides, its cutoff opening over four bars and closing over four.
10DISCO LOOPThe DRUM KIT and the JUNO-106Disco, 120 BPM: four on the floor, a funk bass in octaves, a wah clavinet.
11CHIP LOOPCHIPTUNEChiptune, 125 BPM: a verse and a bridge, chords arpeggiated on one voice.
12HIP-HOP LOOPSWING and LO-FIBoom bap, 86 BPM, SWING 58 %: the DRUM KIT, an acoustic bass, an electric piano, all through the LO-FI.
13DNB LOOPThe BASS and VOICES samplersDrum and bass, 172 BPM: a two-step break, the DNB bass, a pad; then a bridge with the WOBBLE bass.
14ROCK LOOPThe guitarsRock, 126 BPM: power chords and palm mutes, a lead with bends; then a half-time bridge.
15METAL LOOPThe guitarsMetal, 128 BPM: a double kick, a galloping riff, a tremolo-picked line; then a breakdown.
16ELECTRO LOOPThe JUNO-106's 808 soundsElectro, 126 BPM: a broken 808 kick, a sequenced bass, a timpani figure answered by a robotic lead.
17WORLD LOOPThe PERCUSSION samplerWorld house, 120 BPM: darbuka and tabla, an upright bass, a flute melody.

Nine are at 120 to 128 BPM and TRANCE LOOP at 140. HIP-HOP LOOP at 86 BPM and DNB LOOP at 172 make a pair that SYNC matches at half or double (chapter 10).

Specifications

PT/FM on the FM-1, in figures.

Sound

EnginesDX7 (6-operator FM, 32 algorithms), JUNO-106, TB-303, CHIP (8-bit and 16-bit era sound chips), sampler, FUSION (layers of the others, played from a pattern)
Voices16 at most (SETTINGS' VOICES: 8, 12 or 16), shared by the songs, the loops, DJ's decks and the keys; 16 with the second processor running, else 12
InstrumentsCartridges of up to 32 (DX7), 128 (JUNO-106, TB-303, CHIP) or 64 (sampler, FUSION) instruments; 11 built in (F0-FA, 568 instruments), yours numbered 00-EF
Samples8-bit or 16-bit, stored losslessly compressed; up to 64 a sampler cartridge
EffectsGATE, FILTER, DRIVE, LO-FI, CHORUS, DELAY, REVERB, LIMITER, DUCK and the METRONOME, in a chain you order; 16 punch-in effects; a mixer of 16 tracks with three sends
Sample rate44.1 kHz
TuningA4 = 430-450 Hz

Songs, patterns and loops

PatternsUp to 240 (00-EF), each of 1-16 tracks and 1-128 rows
SongsUp to 254 (00-FD), each of 1-256 positions
LoopsUp to 16 at once in LOOPS
DJTwo decks, each a song
TempoTEMPO 3-600 (at 6 ticks a row and 4 rows a beat, the BPM)
Storage412 KB of flash for your work and uploads (a part kept free for saving); unsaved edits in working memory until SAVE

Connections and controls

USBMIDI in and out, class compliant; audio to the computer (UAC1, 16-bit stereo, 44.1 or 48 kHz); installs and uploads from a Chrome or Edge page
MIDI INTRS jack (a TRS-to-DIN adapter, type A or B, for a DIN cable)
OutputStereo output jack (a cable in it mutes the speaker); the built-in speaker (one channel)
Display240 x 240 colour LCD
Controls27 keys (F to G, two octaves and a bit), 14 buttons, 7 endless knobs, MASTER
FirmwarePT/FM, installed over the FM-1's own update path; USB RESCUE (OCT- held at power-on) always there

What PT/FM sends and what it answers to. Transmitted: over USB only (the FM-1 has no MIDI OUT jack). Recognized: over USB and the MIDI IN jack alike. O yes, X no. Chapter 16 explains it all.

FunctionTransmittedRecognizedRemarks
Basic channel: default1ALLSent: MIDI OUT CHANNEL; received: MIDI IN CHANNEL
Basic channel: changed1-16ALL, 1-16With MIDI OUT ALL, track 00-0F on channels 1-16 besides
ModeMode 3Mode 1 (ALL), mode 3 (1-16)
Note number12-1270-127C-0 to G-9 sent. Notes past the keys' range play the current instrument
Velocity: note onOOThe keys send KEYS VOLUME; a track's note its volume
Velocity: note offXXSent as 8n, velocity 0
After touch: keys, channelXX
Pitch bendXOThe keys' notes, plus or minus 2 semitones
Control change 0XOBank select: the n-th cartridge in the list, from 0
Control change 64XOSustain: holds the notes played from MIDI

Mode 1: OMNI ON, POLY. Mode 3: OMNI OFF, POLY. Notes that came in over MIDI are never sent back out.

Glossary

The words this manual uses, each in a line, with where it is explained.

The words

BPM
Beats a minute: how fast a song goes. The screens show it beside TEMPO (chapter 6).
Built-in
What PT/FM itself carries: the eleven synth cartridges F0 to FA. They are there after every install; your changes to them are kept apart, and BACK TO BUILT-IN drops them (chapter 4).
Cartridge
A bank of instruments of one kind (DX7, JUNO-106, TB-303, CHIP, sampler or FUSION), numbered 00 to FF. SEL + PRESETS picks one (chapter 8).
Cell
One track's place on one row: a note, its instrument, its volume and up to four commands (chapter 7).
Command
An instruction in a cell that changes how a note plays (a slide, a vibrato, a volume) or how the song goes (a jump, a tempo), written as a letter or sign and two digits, A04 (chapter 7).
Count-in
One or two bars of clicks before a take starts (chapter 7).
Cue point
Where a DJ deck starts from and goes back to (chapter 10).
Current instrument
The instrument the keys play, shown at the footer's left: PRESETS picks it (chapter 4).
Current song
The song at SONGS' cursor: PLAY plays it, and the EDITOR's loop plays at its tempo (chapter 6).
Deck
One of DJ's two players, each with a song of its own (chapter 10).
Edit memory
Where every change waits until SAVE writes it; switching off loses it (chapter 4).
FUSION
An instrument made of a pattern: each key plays one row of it, every note of that row at once (chapter 8).
FX setup
A song's effects: the chain's order, each effect's knobs and on/off, the mixer and the metronome. LOOPS, DJ and THE KEYS have their own (chapter 15).
Hex
Counting in sixteens, the way trackers number things: 00 to 09, then 0A to 0F, then 10; 7F is 127 (the conventions).
Instrument
A sound in a cartridge's slot, written 01:05 (cartridge 01, slot 05) (chapter 8).
Loop
On LOOPS, a recorded line of notes that repeats; up to 16 play together (chapter 14).
Order
The list of patterns a song plays, one after another (chapter 6).
Pattern
A grid of notes: up to 16 tracks across and 128 rows down, played from top to bottom. Songs are made of patterns (chapter 7).
Position
A place in a song's order, numbered from 00; each position plays one pattern (chapter 6).
Punch-in
An effect played live while a white key is held with FX: a stutter, a tape stop, a filter sweep (chapter 15).
Row
One step in time of a pattern, numbered in hex from 00. With 4 rows a beat, a row is a sixteenth note (chapter 6).
Sample
A recorded sound, kept in a sampler cartridge. An instrument plays it (chapter 8, chapter 17).
Slot
A cartridge's place for one instrument, numbered from 00 (chapter 8).
Song
An order of patterns with its own tempo, mixer and effects (chapter 6).
Take
A live recording in the EDITOR: the pattern plays round and round while what you play is written (chapter 7).
THE KEYS
The keys' own effects and tempo, used before anything has played and after UNLOAD SONG (chapter 15).
Tick
A row's smaller step: a row lasts TICKS A ROW ticks (6 at first), and commands such as slides act on every tick (chapter 6).
Toast
A short message in the header, for two seconds (chapter 3).
Track
A column of a pattern, numbered 00 to 0F; each plays one line of notes, and HOME's combination mutes it (chapter 4).
User area
The FM-1's memory for what you save and upload. An install never writes it (chapter 2).
Voice
One sounding note. PT/FM plays up to 16 at once (SETTINGS' VOICES, chapter 13).
